"That's fun!" Ben says. He takes the other end of the chain and rolls it too. They make the chain go faster and slower.

"Oh no, the chain is stuck!" Lila says. She tries to pull the chain, but it is too tight.

"Let me help you!" Ben says. He tries to push the chain, but it is too hard.

"We were playing with the chain and it got stuck on the chair!" Lila says.

"We can't get it off!" Ben says.

Mommy smiles and hugs them. She says, "Don't worry, I can help you. The chain is not broken, it is just tangled. We just need to untangle it carefully."

She takes the chain and gently unwraps it from the chair leg. She makes sure the rings are not twisted or bent. She gives the chain back to Lila and Ben.

"Here you go, the chain is free now. You can play with it again, but be careful not to get it stuck on anything else, okay?" she says.

"Okay, mommy, thank you!" Lila and Ben say. They hug mommy and say sorry.

He asked his mom for a paper and a crayon, and she gave him a yellow one. He went close to the fence and tried to draw the lion. But the lion was sleeping, and Ben could not see its face. He only saw its big body and its tail.

"Mom, I can't mark the lion's face. It is hiding," Ben said.

"Maybe you can wait until it wakes up, or try to mark another animal," his mom said.

"Yuck! This lemonade is sour. I don't like it," Ben said.

He made a funny face and spit out the lemonade. He threw the cup on the ground and ran back to his mom.

"Mom, the lemonade was sour. It was bad," he said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Maybe you can try some water or juice instead," his mom said.

"Ben, why don't we make a funny face and try to wake up the lion? Maybe it will show us its face then," she said.

The lion heard the noise and opened its eyes. It saw Ben and his mom making funny faces. It was curious and amused. It got up and walked to the fence. It showed them its face and its teeth. It roared back at them.

Ben was happy and excited. He saw the lion's face and its mane. He grabbed his paper and his crayon. He marked the lion as fast as he could. He made a big smile and showed his mom.

"Look, mom, I marked the lion. It is beautiful," he said.

Ben was proud and happy. He thanked the lion for showing him its face. He said goodbye to the lion and waved. He held his mom's hand and walked to the next animal. He wondered what he would mark next. He hoped it would not be sour.

One day, a little girl came to his castle. She wanted to see the king. She knocked on his door, but he did not hear her. She opened the door and saw him sitting on his throne. He was pouring water on his crown.

"Hello, King Leo," she said. "Can I play with you?"

King Leo did not answer. He did not see her. He was looking at his crown.

The little girl walked closer to him. She saw his ears. They were covered with a big cloth. She wondered why.

She touched his shoulder. He jumped. He saw her. He was scared. He did not know who she was.

"Who are you?" he asked. "What do you want?"

"I am Lily," she said. "I want to play with you. Can I see your crown?"

King Leo was surprised. He did not know how to play. He did not have any friends. He only had his crown.

He looked at Lily. She had a big smile. She had bright eyes. She looked kind.

He decided to let her see his crown. He took it off his head and gave it to her.

She took it and thanked him. She put it on her head. She felt like a queen.

She looked at King Leo. She saw that he was deaf. She felt sorry for him.

She wanted to make him happy. She had an idea.

She took his hand and led him to the window. She pointed to the garden. She showed him the flowers, the birds, the bees, the butterflies. She made signs with her hands. She told him their names. She told him they were beautiful.

King Leo watched her. He did not understand her words. But he understood her signs. He understood her smile. He felt something warm in his heart.

He smiled back at her. He felt like a king.

Lily liked to swim. She had a big pool in her backyard. She wore a pink swimsuit and a hat. She had a floaty and a ball. She played with her mom and dad in the water.

One day, it was very hot. Lily wanted to swim, but her mom said no. She said there was a storm coming. She said they had to go inside. Lily was sad. She did not like storms. They were loud and scary.

She went to her room. She looked for something to do. She saw her closet. It was long and dark. She wondered what was inside. She opened the door. She saw some clothes and toys. She also saw a big box. She was curious. She climbed into the box.

She found a book and a flashlight. She turned on the flashlight. She looked at the book. It had pictures of fish and turtles and sharks. It was a book about swimming. Lily smiled. She pretended she was swimming with the animals. She made noises like them. She had fun.

She did not hear the storm outside. She did not hear her mom calling her. She was too busy swimming in the box. She was happy. She liked to swim.

Tommy loves his truck. It is big and red and makes loud noises. He likes to play with it in the yard and pretend he is a driver. He owns his truck and does not share it with anyone.

One day, he sees a new boy in the park. The boy has a truck too, but it is bigger and blue and has lights and sirens. Tommy is envious of the boy's truck. He wants to have it for himself.

He walks over to the boy and says, "Give me your truck. It is better than mine."

The boy looks at Tommy and shakes his head. He says, "No, this is my truck. I own it and I like it. You have your own truck. Go play with it."

Tommy is angry and tries to grab the boy's truck. The boy holds on and they start to fight. They pull and push and shout and cry.

A grown-up sees them and comes over. She says, "Stop fighting, boys. You can't take someone else's truck. That is not nice. You have to share and be friends."

She makes them say sorry to each other and gives them each a cookie. She tells them to play together and take turns with their trucks. Tommy and the boy agree and start to play. They find out they have a lot in common and have fun. They are not envious anymore. They are happy.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were pirates and look for treasure. Tom had a toy gun and Lily had a toy pipe. They wore hats and scarves and said "Arrr" a lot.

They saw a big hill with a hole in it. "Maybe there is treasure in there," Tom said. "Let's go and see." He ran to the hole and pointed his gun inside. "I'll shoot any bad guys who try to stop us," he said.

Lily followed him, but she was a bit scared. She did not like dark places. She put her pipe in her mouth and tried to be calm. "Are you sure this is a good idea, Tom?" she asked.

Tom nodded. "Of course it is. We are brave pirates. Come on, Lily, don't be a chicken." He crawled into the hole and disappeared.

Lily waited for a few seconds, then heard a loud noise. "Bang!" It was Tom's gun. She heard him scream. "Ow! Ow! Ow!"

Lily dropped her pipe and ran to the hole. She saw Tom lying on the ground, holding his foot. He had shot himself by accident. He was crying and bleeding.

Lily felt sorry for him. She forgot her fear and crawled into the hole. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm here. I'll help you. You're not a bad pirate. You're just a silly one."

Tim has a red cap that he likes very much. He wears it every day when he goes out to play. He thinks his cap is very cool and makes him look like a big boy.

One day, he meets a new friend at the park. Her name is Sue and she has a blue dress and long hair. She sees Tim's cap and says, "Hi, I like your cap. Can I try it on?"

Tim is not sure. He likes his cap and does not want to share it. He says, "No, this is my cap. You can't have it."

Sue is sad. She says, "But I just want to try it. I have a doll that you can play with. We can trade for a little while."

Tim thinks about it. He likes dolls too. He says, "OK, but only for a little while. And you have to be careful with my cap. Don't lose it or break it."

Sue smiles. She says, "OK, I promise. Thank you, Tim. You are a nice friend."

They trade their toys and play together. They have fun and laugh. Tim tells Sue stories about his cap and Sue tells Tim stories about her doll. They are happy. They learn to share and be kind.

Tom and Lily were playing knights and dragons in the garden. Tom had a wood sword and Lily had a wood shield. They pretended to fight the big dragon that lived in the bush.

"Roar!" said the dragon, which was really their dog Max. Max liked to play with them and wagged his tail.

"Take that, dragon!" said Tom, swinging his sword. "You are no match for me, the brave knight!"

"Help, help!" said Lily, hiding behind her shield. "The dragon is too strong!"

Max jumped on Lily and licked her face. Lily giggled and dropped her shield. Tom ran to help her, but Max was faster. He grabbed Tom's sword in his mouth and ran away.

"Hey, come back!" said Tom, chasing Max. "That's my sword!"

Max ran to his dog house and lay down with the sword. He looked at Tom and Lily with his big eyes and wagged his tail again.

"Please, dragon, give me back my sword!" said Tom, reaching for the wood. "We want to play some more!"

Max shook his head and growled. He did not want to give up his toy. He liked the wood sword. It was fun to bite and chew.

"Dragon, surrender!" said Lily, trying to sound brave. "Or we will tickle you!"

Max barked and wagged his tail harder. He liked to be tickled. He dropped the sword and rolled over. Tom and Lily tickled his belly and ears. Max licked their faces and paws.

They all laughed and cuddled. They were happy and loyal friends. They did not need a sword or a shield to have fun. They had each other.

Ben and Lily like to play by the river. They have a big box with many toys. They open the box and take out some boats. They put the boats in the water and watch them float.

"Look, my boat is fast!" Ben says. He has a red boat with a sail.

"Mine is pretty!" Lily says. She has a yellow boat with flowers.

They see a big rock in the river. It has a hole in it. Ben has an idea.

"Let's see if our boats can fit in the hole!" he says.

They push their boats to the rock. Ben's boat goes in the hole first. It is small and fit. Lily's boat goes next. It is big and does not fit. It gets stuck.

"Oh no, my boat!" Lily cries.

Ben tries to help. He pulls Lily's boat. It does not move. He pulls harder. It still does not move.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Your boat is too big. It does not fit in the hole." he says.

Lily is sad. She likes her boat. She does not want to lose it.

"Maybe we can find something to make the hole bigger." Ben says.

They look around. They see a stick. They pick it up. They poke the hole with the stick. They make the hole bigger. Lily's boat comes out.

"Yay, my boat!" Lily says.

She hugs her boat. She is happy. She thanks Ben.

"You're welcome, Lily. You're my friend." Ben says.

They smile. They play with their boats again. They have fun by the river.

Sara and Ben like to play with blocks. They make towers and bridges and houses with the blocks. They have many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green, and more.

One day, Sara and Ben want to see who can make the tallest tower. They start to stack the blocks on the floor. Sara uses red blocks and Ben uses blue blocks. They count the blocks as they stack them. "One, two, three, four, five," Sara says. "One, two, three, four, five, six," Ben says.

They keep stacking until they run out of blocks. Then they look at their towers. Sara's tower has ten blocks and Ben's tower has eleven blocks. Ben says, "My tower is taller than yours. I win!"

Sara is sad. She wants her tower to be taller too. She looks around and sees a ruler on the table. She has an idea. She takes the ruler and puts it next to her tower. She sees some small lines on the ruler. She points to them and says, "Look, Ben. These are inches. They are how we measure how tall things are. Let's measure our towers with inches."

Ben agrees. He takes the ruler and puts it next to his tower. He counts the inches. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve," he says. "My tower is twelve inches tall."

Sara puts the ruler next to her tower. She counts the inches. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen," she says. "My tower is thirteen inches tall."

Sara is happy. She says, "My tower is taller than yours in inches. I win!"

Ben is surprised. He says, "How can that be? You have fewer blocks than me."

Sara says, "Because my blocks are bigger than yours. See? One of my blocks is two inches and one of your blocks is one inch. So even if I have fewer blocks, my tower is taller in inches."

Ben says, "Oh, I see. You are right. Your tower is taller in inches. You win!"

Sara and Ben smile at each other. They are both happy. They say, "We both did a good job. Let's make another tower together. We can use all the colors of the blocks." They start to stack the blocks again. They have fun playing with blocks and measuring with inches.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big tree with red fruits. They were hungry and wanted to try them.

"Look, Lily, red fruits! Maybe they are sweet and juicy," Tom said.

"I don't know, Tom. Mommy said we should not eat things we don't know. They might be poison," Lily said.

"Poison? What is poison?" Tom asked.

"Poison is something bad that makes you sick or hurt. Mommy said some plants and animals have poison. We should be careful," Lily said.

Tom was curious and brave. He picked a red fruit and bit it. It was hard and bitter. He spat it out and made a face.

"Yuck! This is not good. This is poison!" Tom said.

Lily was scared and worried. She ran to Tom and hugged him.

"Tom, are you okay? Do you feel sick or hurt?" Lily asked.

Tom shook his head. He felt fine, but he did not like the taste.

"I'm okay, Lily. But I don't want to eat this fruit again. Let's go and find something else to eat," Tom said.

Lily nodded. She was glad Tom was okay. She took his hand and they walked away from the tree.

They saw a man selling ice cream. They smiled and clapped. They liked ice cream. It was sweet and cold.

"Can we have some ice cream, please?" Tom and Lily asked.

The man smiled and gave them each a cone. They thanked him and licked their ice cream.

They forgot about the red fruit. They were happy and full. They played some more in the park. They had a good day.

Lily and Ben were playing with their dolls in the living room. They liked to make up stories and pretend they were the dolls' parents. Lily had a pink doll and Ben had a blue doll.

"Let's go to the park with our babies," Lily said. "They can play on the swings and slide."

"OK," Ben agreed. "But we have to be careful. There are big kids at the park and they might be mean."

They put their dolls in a stroller and walked to the park. They saw some big kids playing soccer on the grass. They looked scary and loud.

"Come on, let's go to the playground," Lily said. "It's safer there."

They pushed the stroller to the playground and found two empty swings. They took their dolls out and put them on the swings. They pushed them gently and made cooing noises.

"Look, they are having fun," Ben said. "They like the swings."

"Yes, they do," Lily said. "They are happy babies."

Suddenly, they heard a voice behind them. It was one of the big kids from the soccer game. He had a mean face and a dirty shirt.

"Hey, what are you doing with those stupid dolls?" he said. "They are for babies. You are too old for dolls. Give them to me."

Lily and Ben felt uncomfortable. They did not like the big kid's voice. It was rude and scary. They did not want to give him their dolls. They loved their dolls.

"No, go away," Lily said. "These are our dolls. We are playing with them. You can't have them."

"Yeah, leave us alone," Ben said. "You are mean. We don't like you."

The big kid laughed. He did not understand why Lily and Ben liked their dolls. He thought they were silly and weak. He wanted to take their dolls and break them.

He reached out his hand and grabbed Lily's pink doll. He pulled it hard and made Lily cry.

"Hey, stop it!" Ben shouted. "That's not nice. Give it back!"

He tried to get the doll back, but the big kid was stronger. He pushed Ben away and ran off with the doll.

Lily and Ben were very sad. They hugged each other and cried. They did not know what to do. They wanted their doll back. They wished the big kid would go away.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many wild animals there, like birds, squirrels and rabbits. Ben and Lily liked to watch them and feed them some bread.

"Look, mom, a big bird!" Ben said, pointing to a crow that landed on a bench. "Can I give it some bread?"

"Sure, but be careful, it might peck you," mom said.

Ben broke a piece of bread and held it out to the crow. The crow flew closer and took the bread from his hand. It made a loud sound and flew away.

"Wow, that was fun!" Ben said.

Lily saw a rabbit hiding under a bush. It had brown fur and long ears. Lily wanted to pet it.

"Can I go to the rabbit, mom?" Lily asked.

"Okay, but be gentle, it might be scared," mom said.

Lily walked slowly to the bush and knelt down. She reached out her hand to the rabbit. The rabbit sniffed her hand and nibbled on her finger.

"Ouch, that hurts!" Lily said.

The rabbit hopped away and disappeared.

"Are you okay, Lily?" mom asked.

"Yes, mom, it's just a little bite," Lily said.

Mom gave Lily a band-aid and a hug.

"Sometimes, wild animals don't know how to be nice," mom said. "They are not like our pets at home. They have to find their own food and shelter. They are poor and have to survive."

"I see, mom," Lily said. "Can we lend them some of our things, like our toys and blankets?"

Mom smiled and shook her head.

"No, sweetie, they don't need our things. They have their own things, like nests and burrows. They are happy in their own way. We can lend them our kindness and respect, though. We can watch them and learn from them, but not bother them or hurt them. Do you understand?"

"Yes, mom, I understand," Lily said.

Ben and Lily nodded and hugged mom. They continued to enjoy the park and the wild animals, but from a safe distance. They learned to appreciate the different ways of living and being in the world.

Tom was restless. He did not like to sit still for a long time. He wanted to run and play and jump. But he had to stay in his seat on the big jet. The jet was flying in the sky, taking him and his mom and dad to a new place.

"Mom, I'm bored," Tom said. "When will we get there?"

"Soon, honey," Mom said. "We have to be patient. The jet is very fast, but the new place is very far."

Tom looked out the window. He saw clouds and blue sky. He wondered what the new place would look like. He hoped it would have a park and a playground and some friends for him.

"Look, Tom," Dad said. "Do you see that? That's the sea. We're almost there."

Tom saw the sparkling water below. He also saw some islands and boats and birds. He felt a little excited. He liked the sea. He wanted to swim and splash and build sand castles.

The jet started to go down. Tom heard a voice on the speaker. It said something he did not understand. But he knew it meant they were going to land soon.

"Tom, we're here," Mom said. "Are you ready?"

Tom nodded. He put on his seat belt. He felt the jet shake and bump as it touched the ground. He heard the wheels screech and the engine roar. He saw the buildings and the cars and the people outside.

The jet stopped. The door opened. Tom and his mom and dad got out of their seats. They took their bags and followed the other people. They walked down a long hall and into a big room.

"Welcome to Hawaii," a lady said. She smiled and gave them each a flower necklace. "Aloha!"

Tom felt the warm air and the sweet smell. He saw the palm trees and the sun and the rainbow. He smiled back at the lady. He felt less restless. He felt happy.

He was ready to explore the new place. He hoped it would be fun. He held his mom's and dad's hands. They walked out of the big room and into a new adventure.

Suddenly, they smelled something bad. They saw smoke coming from the kitchen. They heard their mom scream. They were scared. They did not know what to do.

"Mom, what is happening?" Lily shouted.

"Fire, fire! Get out of the house, now!" Mom yelled back.

Lily and Tom dropped their toys and ran to the door. They saw Mom holding a wet towel and a fragile vase. She had tried to put out the fire on the stove, but it was too big. She had grabbed the vase to save it, because it was a gift from Grandma.

"Come on, hurry!" Mom said. She opened the door and pushed Lily and Tom outside. She followed them and closed the door behind her.

They ran to the street and saw a big red truck with a loud siren. It was the firemen. They came to help. They had a long hose and a big ladder. They sprayed water on the house and climbed to the roof.

Lily and Tom hugged Mom and the vase. They were safe, but they were sad. They hoped their toys and their castle and their dragon were not burned. They hoped their house would be okay. They were in a panic. They did not like the fire and the smoke. They wanted everything to be normal again.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to run, slide and swing. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb it.

They found a branch that was low and strong. They held on to it and pulled themselves up. They felt happy and proud. They looked around and saw many things. They saw birds, flowers and clouds.

They also saw a big, green fruit. It was round and spiky. They did not know what it was. They were curious.

"Look, Max, what is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe it is a ball. Let's get it!" Max said.

They moved closer to the fruit. They reached out their hands. They wanted to touch it.

But when they touched it, they felt a sharp pain. The fruit was not a ball. It was a poky fruit. It poked their palms. It hurt a lot.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Max cried. "This is a terrible fruit! It is not a ball. It is a poky fruit. It pokes our palms. It hurts a lot!"

They let go of the fruit. They climbed down the branch. They ran to their mom. They showed her their palms. They had red dots on them.

Their mom saw their palms. She felt sorry for them. She hugged them and kissed them. She gave them a band-aid and a juice. She told them what the fruit was.

"That is a pineapple, Lily and Max. It is a fruit that you can eat. But you have to peel it first. It has a sweet and juicy inside. But it has a poky and hard outside. You have to be careful with it. It can poke your palms. It can hurt a lot."

Lily and Max nodded. They learned something new. They thanked their mom. They drank their juice. They felt better.

They decided to play something else. They did not want to touch the poky fruit again. They wanted to have fun. They liked to play in the park.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big red plant with green leaves. It had many long strips hanging from it.

"What is that?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Let's see." Lily said. She picked a strip and broke it in half. She gave one piece to Ben and kept the other.

They smelled the strip. It had a strong smell. They put the strip in their mouths and bit it.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" They both cried. The strip was very spicy. It made their tongues burn and their eyes water. They spit out the strip and ran to the house.

"Mama! Mama! Help!" They shouted.

Mama came out and saw them. She saw the strip on the ground. She knew what it was.

"Oh, you poor things. You ate a hot pepper. That's very spicy. You need some water and some milk." She said. She took them inside and gave them a glass of water and a glass of milk. She hugged them and kissed them.

"Are you feeling better?" She asked.

"Yes, Mama. Thank you." They said.

"Next time, don't eat anything you don't know. Ask me first, okay?" She said.

"Okay, Mama. We're sorry." They said.

They learned their lesson. They never ate a hot pepper again.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She liked to see all the different animals, but her favorite was the leopard. The leopard had yellow fur with black spots, and it was very fast and strong.

Mia wanted to get closer to the leopard, so she asked her mom if she could come with her to the fence. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful and not touch the fence. Mia nodded and followed her mom to the fence. She saw the leopard lying on a big rock, licking its paw.

"Hello, leopard!" Mia said. "You are so pretty and cool. Do you like living in the zoo?"

The leopard looked at Mia and blinked. It did not say anything, but it made a soft sound in its throat. Mia thought it was trying to talk to her.

"I wish I could talk to you, leopard," Mia said. "But I don't know your language. Maybe you can teach me some words. How do you say hello in leopard?"

The leopard made another sound, louder this time. Mia tried to copy it, but it was hard. She sounded more like a cat than a leopard.

The leopard seemed to like Mia's attempt. It got up from the rock and walked towards the fence. It stopped a few feet away and stared at Mia with its green eyes.

Mia smiled and said, "You are very brave, leopard. You are not afraid of me. Do you want to be my friend?"

The leopard nodded and rubbed its head against the fence. Mia reached out her hand and touched the leopard's fur. It was soft and warm. She felt happy and excited.

Her mom watched them and said, "Wow, Mia, you are very lucky. The leopard likes you. It must think you are very kind and gentle. You know, the leopard is a very modern animal. It can live in many different places and adapt to different situations. It is very smart and clever."

Mia nodded and said, "I know, mom. The leopard is amazing. I love the leopard. And I think the leopard loves me too."

When they came to the bird house, they saw a big bird with a long neck and legs. It had black and white feathers and a small head. Mom said it was an ostrich.

Tim and Kim screamed and jumped off the slide. They ran to their house, but it was too late. The fire had burned everything. They could not find their mom and dad or their toys or their cat.

They fell to the ground and hugged each other. They were alone and sad. They wished they had never gone to the park. They wished they had stayed with their family. They wished the bell had never rung.

Lily and Ben were playing on the farm. They liked to see the animals and help their grandpa. Grandpa was building a new barn for the cows. He worked hard every day.

One day, Lily and Ben saw that the barn was almost complete. Only a few boards were missing. They wanted to surprise grandpa and finish the barn for him. They found some boards and a hammer and nails. They tried to carry the boards to the barn, but they were too heavy. They tried to hammer the nails, but they were too hard. They tried to climb the ladder, but they were too scared.

They felt helpless. They could not complete the barn. They started to cry. Grandpa heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw them with the boards and the hammer and the nails. He smiled and hugged them.

He said, "Thank you, Lily and Ben, for trying to help me. You are very kind and brave. But building a barn is not easy. It takes a lot of skill and strength and safety. You are too little to do it by yourselves. But you can help me in other ways. You can feed the animals, water the plants, and pick the apples. You can also play and have fun. That is what I want you to do."

Lily and Ben felt better. They said sorry to grandpa for making a mess. Grandpa said it was okay. He said he loved them very much. He took them to the barn and showed them how he completed it. He let them pet the cows and give them names. They were happy and proud. They had a great day on the farm.

Tom and Sue like to play in the yard. They find a lot of junk there. They make toys from the junk. They have fun.

One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a sign. The sign says "Famous Junk Collector". The truck stops in front of their yard. A man gets out. He has a big bag.

"Hello, kids," the man says. "I am here to take your junk. I will make it into art. It will be famous."

Tom and Sue are scared. They do not want to give their junk. They like their junk. They run to their toys. They hug them.

"Please, no," Tom says. "This is our junk. We need it. It is not art. It is ours."

"Sorry, kid," the man says. "This is my job. I have to take the junk. It is not yours. It is trash. You can find more junk later."

The man grabs their toys. He puts them in his bag. He does not care. He shakes the bag. He makes room for more junk.

Tom and Sue cry. They are angry. They are sad. They have no toys. They have no junk. They have no fun.

The man gets in his truck. He drives away. He smiles. He has a lot of junk. He will make it into art. He will be famous.

The end.

Tom and Lily liked to play music. They had a band with their friends. Tom played the drum, Lily played the guitar, Ben played the piano and Amy sang. They had fun making songs and sounds.

One day, they saw a poster for a music contest. The poster said: "Do you have a band? Do you want to win a prize? Come to the park on Saturday and show us your talent!" Tom, Lily, Ben and Amy were excited. They wanted to join the contest and win the prize.

They practiced hard for the contest. They learned a new song and made it sound good. They were ready to go to the park on Saturday. But on Friday, Amy got sick. She had a mild fever and a sore throat. She could not sing.

Tom, Lily and Ben were worried. They called Amy and asked her how she was. Amy said she was sorry, but she could not go to the contest. She said they should find someone else to sing for them.

Tom, Lily and Ben did not want to find someone else. They wanted Amy to sing for them. They said they would wait for her to get better. They said they would not go to the contest without her.

But Amy did not get better. She got worse. She had to go to the hospital. She had a serious infection. She could not talk or sing. She could only whisper.

Tom, Lily and Ben went to visit her in the hospital. They brought her flowers and cards. They told her they missed her and they loved her. They asked her if she would ever sing again.

Amy did not answer. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She never woke up.

The end.

Moral: Life is precious and fragile. Cherish your friends and your gifts. Don't take anything for granted.

Anna loved to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was a princess doll. The princess doll had a pink dress, a shiny crown, and long hair. Anna liked to pretend that she was the princess and the other dolls were her friends.

One day, Anna's mom said, "Anna, we are going to the store. Do you want to come with me?" Anna nodded and grabbed her princess doll. She wanted to show her doll to everyone. She put her doll in her backpack and followed her mom.

At the store, Anna saw many things that she liked. She saw books, toys, candy, and clothes. She wanted to have them all. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I have this? And this? And this?" Her mom said, "No, Anna, you can't have everything. You have to choose one thing. And you have to spend your own money. You have some coins in your piggy bank, remember?"

Anna thought for a moment. She wanted to buy something new, but she also loved her princess doll. She opened her backpack and looked at her doll. Her doll smiled at her. Anna felt happy. She said, "Mom, I don't want to buy anything. I have my princess doll. She is my best friend. I want to spend my time with her."

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "That's very sweet, Anna. I'm proud of you. You know how to be grateful and happy with what you have. You don't need to have more things to be happy. You just need to love and care for your friends. That's what makes you an adorable princess."

Sara loves planes. She has many toys of planes. She likes to make them fly in the air. She wants to be a pilot when she grows up.

One day, Sara sees a new dress in the store. It has a picture of a plane on it. It is blue and white, like the sky. Sara wants to wear the dress. She asks her mom to buy it for her.

"Mom, can I have the dress? It has a plane on it. It is so pretty!" Sara says.

Her mom looks at the dress. It is very expensive. It has many frills and sparkles. It is not modest. Her mom does not like it.

"No, Sara, you cannot have the dress. It is too much money. It is not modest. It is not good for you." Her mom says.

Sara is sad. She does not understand. She loves the dress. She loves the plane. She thinks it is good for her.

"Why not, mom? I love the dress. I love the plane. It is good for me. Please, mom, please!" Sara says.

Her mom shakes her head. She tries to explain.

"Sara, listen to me. The dress is not modest. Modest means not too fancy, not too showy. You are a modest girl. You do not need a dress like that. You have many nice clothes. You have many nice toys. You have many nice things. You should be happy with what you have. You should not want what you do not need." Her mom says.

Sara is still sad. She does not want to listen. She wants the dress. She wants the plane. She thinks she needs it.

"No, mom, no. I need the dress. I need the plane. It is not fair. I want it, I want it, I want it!" Sara says.

She starts to cry. She throws a tantrum. She kicks and screams. She makes a lot of noise.

Her mom is angry. She is tired. She is embarrassed. She does not know what to do.

"Sara, stop it. Stop it right now. You are being very naughty. You are being very rude. You are not listening to me. You are not being grateful. You are not being modest. You are making me very upset. You are making everyone look at us. You are making a scene. You are not getting the dress. You are not getting anything. You are going home. Come on, let's go." Her mom says.

She grabs Sara's hand. She pulls her out of the store. She takes her to the car. She drives her home.

Sara is still crying. She is still angry. She is still sad. She does not have the dress. She does not have the plane. She does not have what she wants.

She does not understand. She does not learn. She does not grow.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to go to the shop with Mum. Mum lets them choose one thing each. Anna likes dolls and Ben likes cars.

One day, they see a big dog outside the shop. The dog is black and has sharp teeth. It barks loud and runs fast. Anna and Ben are scared. They hold Mum's hand tight.

"Mum, can we go home?" Anna asks.

"No, we need to buy some things. Don't worry, the dog won't hurt you. It's just playing," Mum says.

But the dog comes closer and closer. It jumps on a bin and knocks it over. The bin makes a loud noise. Anna and Ben scream.

"Go away, dog!" Ben shouts. He points at the dog with his finger. He tries to be brave.

The dog stops and looks at Ben. It tilts its head and wags its tail. It thinks Ben wants to play.

"Good boy, Ben. You are very brave," Mum says. She smiles and pets the dog. The dog licks her hand.

"Can we pet the dog too, Mum?" Anna asks.

"Sure, if you want to. The dog is friendly. He just wants some attention," Mum says.

Anna and Ben pet the dog too. The dog is soft and warm. He likes them. Anna and Ben are not scared anymore. They are happy.

They go to the shop and buy some things. Anna chooses a doll and Ben chooses a car. They also buy a bone for the dog. They give it to him and say goodbye.

"Thank you, dog. You are nice. We hope to see you again," Anna and Ben say.

The dog wags his tail and barks. He is happy too. He runs away with his bone.

Anna and Ben go home with Mum. They play with their doll and car. They tell Dad about the dog. They are proud of being brave.

Tom likes to zip on his bike. He has a red bike with big wheels and a bell. He rides his bike every day in the park with his mom and dad. He likes to go fast and feel the wind on his face.

One day, he sees a big hill in the park. He wants to zip down the hill and see how fast he can go. He asks his mom and dad if he can try it. They say yes, but they tell him to be careful and wear his helmet. They also tell him to watch out for the rocks and the trees at the bottom of the hill.

Tom puts on his helmet and gets on his bike. He pedals hard and starts to zip down the hill. He feels very happy and excited. He goes faster and faster. He thinks he is the fastest bike rider in the world.

But he does not see the big rock on the ground. He hits the rock with his front wheel and falls off his bike. He lands on the ground with a thud. He feels a lot of pain in his knee and his elbow. He starts to cry.

His mom and dad run to him and hug him. They check his knee and his elbow and see that they are bleeding. They clean his wounds and put band-aids on them. They tell him that he is brave and that they are proud of him. They also tell him that he should be more careful next time and look where he is going.

Tom says he is sorry and that he loves them. He also says he still likes to zip on his bike, but maybe not so fast. He learns a lesson that day. He learns that zipping is fun, but zipping too fast can be dangerous. He also learns that his mom and dad are always there for him.

"He is a hero. He fought bad people with his spear," Sam said.

"Can I hold his spear?" Lila said.

Lila did not listen. She climbed on the statue and grabbed the spear. It was very heavy and hard. She lost her balance and fell down. The spear fell with her and made a loud noise.

"Are you okay? Do you need a band-aid?" Sam said.

Lila nodded. She was in pain and sad. She dropped the spear and hugged Sam.

"I'm sorry. I was silly. I should have listened to you," Lila said.

They walked to the nurse's office. The sun was setting and it was getting dark. They held hands and hoped that the hero would not be angry with them.

One day, Lily found a big jar of peanuts in the kitchen. She was very happy. She opened the jar and took a handful of peanuts. She put them in her mouth and chewed. But then, she felt something wrong. Her mouth started to itch and hurt. Her throat felt tight and hard to breathe. Her face turned red and swollen. She dropped the jar and ran to her mom.

Mom saw Lily and was very scared. She saw the jar of peanuts and knew what happened. She grabbed Lily and her phone and called for help. She said, "My daughter ate peanuts and she is allergic. Please come fast!" She tried to calm Lily and make her breathe.

But help did not come fast enough. The peanuts made Lily very sick. She could not breathe at all. She closed her eyes and stopped moving. Mom cried and hugged Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I love you."

Lily did not improve. She did not wake up. She did not eat peanuts anymore. She did not do anything anymore. She was gone. Mom was very sad. She missed Lily every day. She wished she had never bought the jar of peanuts. She wished she had seen the orange sticker on the jar that said, "Warning: Contains Peanuts."

"What happened here?" she asked.

"Ben did not help me with the tray. He was mean," Sara said.

"I wanted to make more food. Sara was bossy," Ben said.

Grandma sighed. She loved her grandchildren, but they did not always get along.

"Listen, Sara and Ben. You need to share and help each other. Playing is more fun when you are nice to each other. And you need to be careful with the tray. It is not a toy. It is for grown-ups. I do not permit you to use it without asking me first. Do you understand?" she said.

Lily and Ben are playing hide and seek in the garden. Lily is the seeker and Ben is the hider. Lily counts to ten and then looks for Ben. She sees a big bush with green leaves. She thinks Ben might be hiding there.

She walks to the bush and peeks behind it. She does not see Ben, but she sees something else. She sees a bowl of salad on a table. The salad has lettuce, tomatoes, carrots and cheese. It looks yummy. Lily loves salad.

She forgets about Ben and goes to the table. She picks up a fork and starts to eat the salad. She thinks it is the best salad ever. She does not hear Ben calling her name.

Ben is hiding under a blanket in the shed. He waits for Lily to find him. He waits and waits, but Lily does not come. He wonders where she is. He gets bored and cold. He decides to give up and look for Lily.

He comes out of the shed and sees Lily eating salad at the table. He is surprised and angry. He says, "Lily, what are you doing? You are supposed to find me, not eat salad! That is not fair!"

Lily runs away and looks for a good hiding spot. She hopes Ben will find her soon. She also hopes there is no more salad in the garden. She has had enough.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree with a swing and a slide. One day, they saw a bee flying near the tree. They wanted to see where it went.

"Look, a bee!" Anna said. "Let's follow it!"

"OK, but be careful. Bees can sting!" Ben said.

They ran after the bee, but it was too fast. They lost it behind some flowers. They looked around, but they could not find it.

"Where did it go?" Anna asked.

"Maybe it went to its home. Bees live in hives and make honey," Ben said.

"Honey? What is honey?" Anna asked.

"Honey is sweet and sticky. You can eat it on bread or with milk. Mommy sometimes gives us honey when we are sick," Ben said.

"I want to try honey. Do you think the bee will share?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we can ask it nicely," Ben said.

They walked around the garden, looking for the bee. They saw many flowers and butterflies, but no bee. They were about to give up, when they heard a buzzing sound. They looked up and saw the bee. It was flying near a hole in the tree.

"Look, there it is!" Anna said. "Maybe that's its home!"

They ran to the tree and gazed at the hole. They saw many bees going in and out. They smelled something sweet.

"Is that honey?" Anna asked.

"I think so. It smells good," Ben said.

They wanted to taste the honey, but they were afraid of the bees. They did not want to get stung.

"Hello, bee!" Anna said. "Can we have some honey, please?"

The bee did not answer. It flew away.

"Maybe it did not hear us," Ben said. "Let's try again."

"Hello, bees!" Anna and Ben said together. "Can we have some honey, please?"

The bees did not answer. They flew around the hole.

"Maybe they are busy," Ben said. "Maybe they need the honey for themselves."

"Maybe they are not normal bees," Anna said. "Maybe they are mean bees."

They felt sad. They wanted to try the honey, but they did not want to make the bees angry.

"Let's go back to the swing and the slide," Ben said. "Maybe we can find some honey later."

"OK," Anna said. "Maybe Mommy has some honey at home."

They left the tree and the bees. They played on the swing and the slide. They had fun, but they still wondered what honey tasted like.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play in the park. They saw a big bench. They wanted to sit on it. But the bench was too high for them.

They had an idea. They found a big stick. They put the stick under the bench. They pushed hard. They wanted to raise the bench. They thought they were smart.

But they were not smart. The stick broke. The bench fell down. It hit Tom and Sam. They cried loud. They were hurt. They were not glad.

A lady heard them. She ran to help them. She called their moms. Their moms came fast. They were angry. They scolded Tom and Sam. They took them home. They put bandages on them. They said no more park for a week.

Tom and Sam were sorry. They learned a lesson. They said they would not raise benches again. They hoped to be friends again. But they were not sure. They were sad.

Lily and Ben like to play in Grandma's attic. They find many old things there. They see an ancient purse on a shelf. It is brown and has a shiny lock.

"Let's open it!" Lily says. She climbs on a chair and takes the purse. Ben helps her. They try to open the lock, but it is too hard.

"Maybe there is a key," Ben says. They look around the attic. They see a box with many keys. They enter the box and take out some keys. They try them on the lock, but none of them fit.

They hear Grandma coming up the stairs. They hurry to put the purse and the keys back. They hide behind a curtain.

"Hello, my dears," Grandma says. She sees the purse on the shelf. She smiles. "Do you want to see what's inside?"

She takes the purse and opens it with a key from her pocket. She shows Lily and Ben what's inside. There are some old photos, a necklace, a coin, and a letter.

"These are things from my mother," Grandma says. "She gave me this purse when I was a little girl. She told me stories about them. Do you want to hear some?"

Lily and Ben nod. They come out from behind the curtain. They sit with Grandma and listen to her stories. They forget about the lock. They are happy.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big ball on the grass. It was red and shiny and looked very fun.

"Let's play with the ball!" Lily said.

"But it is not our ball," Ben said. "Maybe someone left it here by mistake. We should not take it."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to play with the ball. She picked it up and ran away. Ben followed her, feeling sad.

They played with the ball for a while, but then they heard a voice. It was a boy who was looking for his ball. He was crying and asking for help.

"That is the boy who owns the ball," Ben said. "We should give it back to him. He is very sad."

Lily did not want to give the ball back. She liked the ball too much. She hid behind a tree and hoped the boy would not see her.

Ben was honest and kind. He felt sorry for the boy. He suggested to Lily that they should do the right thing and return the ball.

"Lily, please come out. We should not keep the ball. It is not ours. It is his. He loves the ball. We should make him happy."

Lily thought about what Ben said. She realized that he was right. She felt bad for being selfish and mean. She came out from behind the tree and gave the ball back to the boy.

The boy was very happy and thanked them. He smiled and asked them if they wanted to play with him and his ball. Lily and Ben agreed and they all became friends.

The moral of the story is: Be honest and kind. Do not take what is not yours. Share and make others happy.

Lily woke up in the morning and saw a weird thing on her bed. It was a big, round, yellow ball with a smiley face on it. She did not know where it came from or who gave it to her. She picked it up and hugged it. It felt soft and warm.

She got out of bed and went to the kitchen, where her mom was making breakfast. She showed her the ball and said, "Look, mom, I have a new friend!"

Mom looked at the ball and smiled. She said, "That's nice, Lily. What's his name?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "His name is Sunny. He makes me happy."

Mom said, "That's a good name for him. Do you want to take him with you to the park today?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to play with Sunny and show him the swings and the slide and the sandbox."

Mom said, "Okay, but be careful with him. He might get dirty or lost or popped."

Lily said, "Don't worry, mom. I will take good care of Sunny. He is my best friend."

They finished breakfast and got ready to go to the park. Lily put Sunny in her backpack and zipped it up. She held mom's hand and walked to the door. She was very excited to have fun with Sunny.

But when they opened the door, they saw something that made them gasp. It was raining outside. Big, cold, wet drops were falling from the sky and splashing on the ground. Lily did not like rain. It made her sad and cold and wet.

She looked at mom and said, "Mom, what about Sunny? He can't go out in the rain. He will get wet and sad and popped."

Mom looked at Lily and said, "You're right, Lily. Sunny can't go out in the rain. We have to leave him here until the rain stops. Maybe we can find something else to do inside."

Lily felt a tear roll down her cheek. She did not want to leave Sunny. She wanted to play with him and make him happy. She opened her backpack and took out Sunny. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Sunny. I can't take you to the park today. But I will come back for you soon. I love you, Sunny."

She put Sunny back in her backpack and zipped it up. She put the backpack on her bed and said, "Bye, Sunny. See you later."

She took mom's hand and walked to the living room. She tried to smile, but she felt a weird feeling in her chest. She missed Sunny already. She hoped the rain would stop soon. She hoped Sunny would be okay. She hoped he would still be her friend.

One day, she wanted to show her fashion to her friend Tom, who lived next door. She put her dolls in a basket and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Tom opened it.

"Hi, Lisa. What do you have in your basket?" Tom asked.

"My dolls. I want to show you my fashion. Can I come in?" Lisa said.

"Sure, come in. But I don't like dolls. They are boring. I like cars and trucks. They are fun and fast." Tom said.

Lisa followed Tom to his room. He had many cars and trucks on the floor. He picked one up and made a loud noise.

"Vroom, vroom. Look at my car. It can go very fast and jump over anything." Tom said.

Lisa put her basket on the bed and took out one of her dolls. She put a pink dress and a hat on her.

"Look at my doll. She is very pretty and fancy. She can go to a party and dance with anyone." Lisa said.

Tom looked at her doll and made a face.

"Yuck. That is not fun. That is silly. Your doll is lazy. She does not do anything. She just sits there and looks at herself." Tom said.

Lisa felt angry and sad. She did not like what Tom said. She liked her doll and her fashion. She thought Tom was mean and rude.

"No, she is not lazy. She is nice and smart. She can do many things. She can sing and read and draw. She can manage anything. You are mean and rude. You don't know anything about fashion." Lisa said.

Tom and Lisa started to argue. They raised their voices and said mean things to each other. They did not want to play together anymore.

They heard a knock on the door. It was Tom's mom.

"What is going on here? Why are you shouting at each other?" Tom's mom asked.

Tom and Lisa stopped arguing and looked at Tom's mom. They felt ashamed and sorry.

"We were playing with our toys, but we did not like each other's toys. We said mean things to each other. We are sorry." Tom and Lisa said.

Tom's mom smiled and hugged them.

"It's okay. You don't have to like the same things to be friends. You can like different things and still respect and appreciate each other. You can learn from each other and have fun together. Why don't you try to play with each other's toys and see what you can do with them?" Tom's mom said.

Tom and Lisa nodded and smiled. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to give each other's toys a chance. They played with the dolls and the cars and trucks. They found out that they could have fun with both. They made stories and games with them. They laughed and enjoyed themselves. They learned something new about fashion and speed. They became better friends.

Lily was sick. She had a hot head and a sore throat. Mommy gave her some juice and a thermometer. The thermometer was a stick that could tell how hot Lily was.

"Put this under your tongue and wait a bit," Mommy said. "Then I can see if you need medicine."

Lily did what Mommy said. She held the stick in her mouth and closed her eyes. She felt sleepy and bored. She wondered what her brother Ben was doing. He was not sick. He was playing with his cars in his room.

Lily decided to go and see Ben. She was careful not to drop the stick. She got out of bed and walked to the door. She opened it and saw Ben on the floor with his cars.

"Hi, Lily," Ben said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Lily nodded. She liked cars. She forgot about the stick in her mouth. She was careless. She ran to Ben and sat down next to him. She picked up a red car and made it zoom.

"Vroom, vroom," she said.

Suddenly, the stick fell out of her mouth. It hit the floor and broke. The glass cracked and the liquid spilled.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Mommy's stick!"

Ben looked at the broken stick. He saw the liquid. He was curious. He touched it with his finger. It was cold and wet.

"What is this?" he asked.

Lily did not know. She was scared. She thought Mommy would be angry. She started to cry.

"Mommy, Mommy!" she called.

Mommy heard Lily's cry. She came to the room. She saw the broken stick and the liquid. She saw Lily and Ben. She was worried.

"What happened?" she asked.

Lily and Ben told Mommy what happened. They said they were sorry. They did not mean to break the stick.

Mommy hugged them. She was not angry. She was glad they were not hurt. She told them the stick was a thermometer. She told them the liquid was mercury. She told them mercury was bad. She told them not to touch it or eat it.

She took them to the bathroom. She washed their hands and mouths. She threw away the broken thermometer. She cleaned the floor. She got a new thermometer. She checked Lily's temperature. She gave her some medicine. She told them to be careful next time.

She took them back to bed. She read them a story. She kissed them good night. She turned off the light.

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They learned a lesson. They discovered something new. They loved Mommy. They fell asleep.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play games. One day, they decided to play a game with the mailman. They made a trap with a big box and a string. They put a sign on the box that said "Free Candy". They hid behind a bush and waited for the mailman to come.

"Ha ha, we got you!" Ben shouted.

"Help, help, let me out!" the mailman cried.

Ben and Sam felt sorry for the mailman. They lifted the box and helped him out. The mailman was angry and scared. He had a long scratch on his arm from the box.

"That was not funny, that was mean!" the mailman said. "You could have hurt me or made me lose my letters. Do you know how important it is to deliver the mail?"

Ben and Sam looked at the mailman's bag. It was open and some letters had fallen out. They saw one letter that had their name and address on it. It was from their grandma, who lived far away. They loved their grandma and always waited for her letters.

"We're sorry, Mr. Mailman," Sam said. "We didn't mean to make you angry or hurt you. We just wanted to play a game."

"Well, it was a bad game," the mailman said. "You should never play with traps or other people's things. You should be nice and respectful. Here, take your letter and go home. And don't do this again, or I'll tell your parents."

Ben and Sam took their letter and said sorry again. They ran home and opened the letter. It had a picture of their grandma and a note that said "I miss you and love you very much. I'm sending you a big surprise in the mail. I hope you like it."

Ben and Sam felt happy and sad at the same time. They were happy to hear from their grandma and curious about the surprise. But they were sad that they had been mean to the mailman and almost ruined his job. They learned their lesson and never played with traps again. They also wrote a letter to their grandma and the mailman to say thank you and sorry.

Lily liked to eat prunes. She said they were sweet and good for her tummy. She always asked her mom for more prunes after dinner.

One day, Lily saw a big jar of prunes on the kitchen counter. She wanted to reach it, but it was too high for her. She saw a chair nearby and had an idea. She pushed the chair to the counter and climbed on it. She was very happy. She grabbed the jar and opened it.

But she did not see that the jar was too heavy for her. She lost her balance and fell off the chair. The jar also fell and broke on the floor. Prunes and glass were everywhere. Lily was scared and hurt. She cried very loud.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw the mess and Lily on the floor. She was very worried and angry. She picked up Lily and checked her for cuts. She hugged her and said, "Lily, what did you do? You could have been very hurt. You should not push the chair and climb on it. You should ask me for help. That jar was too big for you. You are not strong enough to hold it."

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted more prunes. I like them very much. I thought I was strong enough to get them. I did not mean to break the jar and make a mess."

Her mom said, "I know you like prunes, but you have to be careful and listen to me. Prunes are good for you, but too many prunes are not good. They can make you sick. You have to eat other things too. And you have to share the prunes with your dad and brother. They like them too. Next time, if you want more prunes, just ask me. I will give you some if you are good and polite. And you have to help me clean up this mess."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I love you. I will help you clean up. And I will share the prunes with dad and brother. And I will not push the chair and climb on it again."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are a good girl. And you are strong in your heart. But you have to be smart and safe too. Come on, let's clean up and have some milk and cookies."

The moral of the story is: You should not do things that are dangerous or greedy. You should ask for help and share with others. You should be careful and listen to your parents.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the park. They had a big red ball that they kicked and threw to each other. One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was black and hairy and had sharp teeth. It barked loudly and ran towards them.

"Run, Tim, run!" Kim shouted. She grabbed the ball and ran away from the dog. Tim followed her, but he was slower. He tripped over a shoe that someone had left on the grass. He fell down and hurt his knee. He cried out in pain.

The dog saw Tim on the ground and ran faster. It wanted to bite him and take his shoe. Tim was scared and did not know what to do. He saw Kim running back to him with a stick. She tried to scare the dog away.

"Go away, bad dog! Leave my brother alone!" Kim yelled. She waved the stick at the dog. The dog did not like the stick. It growled and snapped at Kim. It bit the stick and broke it in half.

Kim dropped the stick and backed away. She was scared too. She looked at Tim and said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I tried to help you. Maybe we should surrender and give the dog the shoe. Maybe it will leave us alone then."

Tim shook his head. He did not want to give the dog his shoe. He liked his shoe. It was blue and shiny and had a star on it. He had got it for his birthday. He said, "No, Kim. Don't give the dog my shoe. It's my shoe. It's not fair. Maybe someone will come and save us. Maybe Mom or Dad or the park man."

But no one came. The dog was too big and too loud. No one heard Tim and Kim's cries. No one saw them in the corner of the park. The dog got closer and closer. It jumped on Tim and bit his shoe. It pulled it off his foot and ran away with it. Tim screamed and cried. Kim screamed and cried. They hugged each other and waited for someone to find them.

But no one did. The dog came back. It wanted the other shoe. It wanted the ball. It wanted Tim and Kim. It was hungry and angry. It attacked them and hurt them. It did not stop until they were quiet and still.

One day, they found a big bowl of flour in the kitchen. They wondered what it was for. They decided to mix it with water and make some dough. They thought it would be fun to make shapes with the dough and put them on the motor.

They poured some water into the bowl and stirred it with a spoon. They made a sticky mess. They took some dough and rolled it into balls and snakes and stars. They stuck them on the motor and smiled.

"Look, Lily, a dolphin!" Tom said, pointing to a gray shape.

"Wow, Tom, it's so pretty!" Lily said, clapping her hands.

They ran to the edge of the harbor, trying to get closer to the dolphin. They did not see the sign that said "Danger. Do not go near the water."

A bad man saw them. He had a big bag and a net. He wanted to catch the dolphin and sell it. He followed Tom and Lily quietly.

"Hey, kids, do you want to see the dolphin better?" he said, pretending to be nice.

Tom and Lily turned around and saw the bad man. They felt scared. They did not know him.

"No, thank you, mister. We have to go home now," Tom said, holding Lily's hand.

The bad man did not listen. He grabbed Tom and Lily and put them in his bag. He threw the net over the dolphin and dragged it to his boat.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily shouted, kicking and crying.

The dolphin heard them. It was very smart and brave. It bit the net and broke free. It swam to the boat and pushed it with its nose. The boat tipped over and the bad man fell into the water.

Tom and Lily crawled out of the bag. They saw the dolphin smiling at them. They smiled back and said, "Thank you, dolphin. You are our friend."

The dolphin nodded and waved its tail. It swam away, happy and free.

Tom and Lily ran back to the harbor. They found their mom and dad, who were looking for them. They hugged them and told them what happened.

Mom and dad were very angry at the bad man and very proud of the dolphin. They were also very happy that Tom and Lily were safe.

They said, "Tom and Lily, you did a good job. But you have to be careful. Do not follow strangers. And do not go near the water without us. The harbor can be dangerous."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We're sorry, mom and dad. We love you. And we love the dolphin."

They all went home, happy and grateful.

Lily looked around. She did not see anyone near the bench. "Maybe we can, but we have to be careful. It is not ours."

"Let's pretend we won it for being the best at something," Ben said.

They put the trophy on the ground and started to jump. They jumped high and low, fast and slow. They laughed and had fun.

He saw Lily and Ben jumping with his trophy. He was angry and sad.

"Hey, that's my trophy!" he shouted. "Give it back to me!"

Lily and Ben stopped jumping. They were scared and sorry. They did not know it was his trophy.

"We are sorry, mister," Lily said. "We did not know it was yours. We just wanted to play with it."

"It's not a toy, it's a trophy," the man said. "I won it for running a race. It is very important to me."

He took the trophy from them and put it back on the bench. He looked at it closely. He saw a scratch on the star.

"What did you do to my trophy?" he asked. "You scratched it!"

Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not mean to scratch it.

"We are sorry, mister," Ben said. "We did not see the scratch. We did not want to hurt your trophy."

The man sighed. He was still angry, but he saw that they were sorry.

"Look, I know you did not mean to do it, but you have to be more careful," he said. "You can't just take things that are not yours. You have to ask first. And you have to replace them if you break them."

"What does replace mean?" Lily asked.

"It means to give something new or good for something old or bad," the man said. "For example, if you break a toy, you have to give a new toy or fix the old toy. Or if you eat a cookie, you have to give another cookie or share something else."

"Oh, we understand," Ben said. "But we don't have anything to replace your trophy. We don't have any money or other trophies."

The man thought for a moment. He did not want to be mean to them, but he also wanted his trophy to be nice.

"OK, I have an idea," he said. "You can help me replace my trophy by doing something nice for me. How about you help me carry it to my car? It is very heavy and I have a bad back."

Lily and Ben nodded. They wanted to help him. They felt sorry for scratching his trophy.

"OK, mister, we will help you," Lily said.

"Thank you, kids," the man said. "That is very kind of you. Come on, let's go."

"Thank you again, kids," the man said. "You are very good helpers. And I'm sorry for yelling at you. I was just surprised and upset."

"It's OK, mister," Ben said. "We are sorry for taking your trophy. We won't do it again."

The man smiled. He gave them each a high five and a candy.

"Here, this is for you," he said. "You can have it as a reward for being nice and helpful. And maybe one day, you will win your own trophy for something you are good at."

Lily and Ben smiled. They thanked him and took the candy. They waved goodbye to him as he drove away.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned not to take things that are not theirs. They learned to be careful with other people's things. And they learned to replace them if they break them.

They also learned that being nice and helpful can make someone happy. And that sometimes, a candy can be better than a trophy.

"I'm sorry, mom, I wanted to help you, but I struggled with the plate. It was too big for me," Lily said, feeling sad.

"It's okay, Lily, I know you meant well, but you have to be careful. Washing the dishes is not for little girls. You could hurt yourself or make a mess. Why don't you help me with something else?" her mom said, hugging her.

"Like what, mom?" Lily asked, wiping her tears.

"Well, you can help me by turning off the tap. That way, we can save water and be useful to the earth. Water is very important and we should not waste it. Do you know how to turn off the tap?" her mom asked, pointing to the faucet.

"Yes, mom, I know. You have to twist it like this," Lily said, reaching for the tap. She turned it off and stopped the water from running.

"Good job, Lily, you are very smart and helpful. Thank you for turning off the tap. You are saving water and being useful to the earth. That makes me very proud of you," her mom said, smiling.

"Thank you, mom, I love you. Can I help you with something else?" Lily asked, feeling happy.

"Sure, Lily, you can help me by drying the dishes with this towel. That way, we can finish faster and have more time to play. How does that sound?" her mom asked, handing her a towel.

"That sounds great, mom. I like to dry the dishes. It's easy and fun. And I like to play with you. You are the best mom ever," Lily said, taking the towel and drying the dishes.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that helping others is good, but we have to be careful and choose tasks that are suitable for our age and abilities. It also teaches that saving water is useful and important for the earth.

The teacher said, "Sam, why did you erase Tom and Lily's drawings? They worked hard on them. They were proud of them. How would you feel if someone erased your work?"

Sam felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I don't know. I was bored. I wanted to have fun. But I was not fun. I was rude. I am sorry, teacher. I am sorry, Tom and Lily."

The teacher said, "I am glad you are sorry, Sam. But sorry is not enough. You need to make it up to them. You need to help them draw again. You need to be kind and respectful. Can you do that?"

Sam nodded. He said, "Yes, teacher. I can do that. I want to be a good friend. I want to learn to draw too."

"Because I want to be a butterfly," the caterpillar said. "Butterflies are beautiful and can fly. I think flying is fun."

Lily and Ben were amazed. They did not know that caterpillars could become butterflies.

"Wow, that is amazing," Lily said. "How do you become a butterfly?"

"I need to make a cocoon," the caterpillar said. "A cocoon is a cozy shell where I can change. It takes a long time, but when I come out, I will have wings and colors."

"Can we see you when you come out?" Ben asked.

"Of course," the caterpillar said. "But you have to be patient and wait. And you have to be gentle and not touch my cocoon. It is very delicate."

One day, a little girl named Lily wanted to make a card for her grandma. She had some paper, some crayons, and some stickers. She drew a picture of her and her grandma on the paper. She wrote "I love you" with her crayons. She put some stickers on the card to make it pretty.

She looked at her card and smiled. She wanted to make it more special. She saw a ribbon on the table. It was red and shiny. She thought it would make a nice bow. She tried to tie the ribbon into a bow, but it was hard. She asked her mom for help.

"Mom, can you help me make a bow?" she said.

"Sure, Lily. What are you making?" her mom said.

"I'm making a card for grandma. I want to put a bow on it," Lily said.

"That's very sweet of you, Lily. Here, let me show you how to make a bow. You take the ribbon and make two loops. Then you cross them over and pull them tight. Then you make a knot and fluff the loops. See? You have a bow," her mom said.

"Wow, thank you, mom. You are very useful," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Lily. You are very clever," her mom said.

Lily put the bow on her card. She looked at it and smiled. She thought it was the best card ever. She wanted to give it to her grandma right away. She put the card in an envelope. She saw a stamp on the table. It was blue and had a picture of a bird. She thought it would make a nice stamp. She stuck the stamp on the envelope.

"Mom, can you help me mail the card?" she said.

"Sure, Lily. What are you mailing?" her mom said.

"I'm mailing a card for grandma. I put a stamp on it," Lily said.

"That's very nice of you, Lily. But this stamp is not for mailing. This stamp is for collecting. It is very old and rare. It is worth a lot of money," her mom said.

"Oh, I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. I just thought it was pretty," Lily said.

"It's okay, Lily. You didn't mean to. But you have to be careful with stamps. Some stamps are for mailing and some stamps are for collecting. You have to ask before you use them," her mom said.

"I understand, mom. I will ask next time. Can we get another stamp for mailing?" Lily said.

"Of course, Lily. We can get another stamp for mailing. Come on, let's go to the post office. I'm sure grandma will love your card," her mom said.

Lily and her mom went to the post office. They got another stamp for mailing. It was green and had a picture of a flower. Lily thought it was pretty too. She stuck it on the envelope. She gave the envelope to the mailman. She waved goodbye to her card.

"Bye, card. I hope you make grandma happy," she said.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of being careful with other people's things and asking before using them. It also shows the value of being creative, loving, and grateful.

"La la la, I am a sailor, I love the sea, I catch the fish, la la la."

But he was also very careless. He did not look at the sky or the water. He did not see the dark clouds or the big waves. He did not hear the wind or the thunder.

Soon, a storm started. The rain poured and the lightning flashed. The boat rocked and the sailor was scared.

"Help, help, I am a sailor, I hate the sea, I lose the fish, help, help."

He saw another boat nearby. It was bigger and stronger than his boat. He waved his arms and shouted.

"Help, help, please help me, I am a sailor, I am in trouble, help, help."

The other boat saw him and came closer. It was a coast guard boat. The coast guard was brave and kind. He threw a rope to the sailor and pulled him in.

"Are you okay, sailor? You are very careless. You should not sail in a storm. You should watch the weather and be careful."

The sailor was ashamed and grateful. He thanked the coast guard and said sorry.

"Thank you, thank you, you are very brave and kind. I am sorry, I am very careless. I will not sail in a storm again. I will watch the weather and be careful."

The coast guard smiled and nodded. He took the sailor and his boat back to the shore. The sailor hugged his family and learned his lesson. He was still a sailor, but he was not careless anymore. He was happy and careful.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big, yellow butterfly. It was flying from flower to flower.

"Look, a butterfly!" Tom said. "I want to catch it!"

He ran after the butterfly, but it was too fast. He tried to jump and grab it, but it flew away.

"Tom, stop!" Lily said. "You can't catch a butterfly. You will hurt it!"

But Tom was persistent. He did not listen to Lily. He wanted to catch the butterfly.

He saw a rope on the ground. He had an idea. He picked up the rope and made a loop. He tried to throw the loop over the butterfly, like a cowboy.

But the butterfly was smart. It saw the rope and dodged it. The loop missed the butterfly and landed on Tom's head. It was tight and tangled.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "Help me, Lily! The rope is hurting me!"

Lily ran to Tom. She saw the rope on his head. She tried to untie it, but it was hard.

"Tom, you were silly," Lily said. "You should not try to catch a butterfly. You should be nice to it. It is a living thing, like you and me."

She pulled and pulled on the rope. Finally, she untied it. She took it off Tom's head.

Tom was sorry. He rubbed his head. He looked at the butterfly. It was still flying in the garden, happy and free.

"I'm sorry, butterfly," Tom said. "You are beautiful. I will not bother you again."

He smiled at Lily. She smiled back. They hugged.

They decided to watch the butterfly, not catch it. They sat on the grass and admired it. They learned to respect it. They were happy.

Her mom said no, because it's not normal to eat unwashed blueberries. Lily didn't understand why it wasn't normal, so she asked her mom to explain.

Her mom said, "Eating unwashed blueberries could make you sick. It's important to pause and take the time to wash them so they are clean and safe to eat." Lily understood and patiently waited for her mom to wash the blueberries. When they were clean, Lily happily ate them all up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a furry cat named Mittens. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help her hang up some new curtains in the living room. Lily was excited to help and climbed up on a chair to reach the curtain rod.

But then, something embarrassing happened. Lily accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke into a million pieces. Her mom wasn't mad, but Lily felt embarrassed. "I'm sorry, Mommy," she said.

"It's okay, Lily," her mom said. "Accidents happen. Let's clean it up together." And so, they cleaned up the mess and hung up the curtains. Mittens even helped by batting around some of the broken pieces. In the end, Lily felt proud that she helped and wasn't embarrassed anymore.
