But Benny didn't listen to Ollie's urge to stop eating so much honey. He kept eating and eating until he felt very sick. He knew he needed to go to the port to find a remedy for his tummy ache.

On his way to the port, Benny met a friendly rabbit named Remy. Remy offered to help Benny find a cure for his tummy ache. Together, they searched the port until they found a special herb that would make Benny feel better.

Benny learned his lesson and promised to listen to his friends' advice in the future. From that day on, he only ate a little bit of honey each day and never got sick again.

Lily loves spaghetti. She likes to twirl it on her fork and slurp it in her mouth. She likes to make funny noises with the sauce. She likes to eat it with cheese and meatballs.

One day, Lily's mom makes spaghetti for dinner. She puts a big plate of spaghetti on the table. She tells Lily to be careful and not make a mess. Lily nods and smiles. She is very hungry.

Lily picks up her fork and starts to eat. She twirls a long strand of spaghetti on her fork. She lifts it to her mouth. But then, she slips. Her fork falls from her hand. The spaghetti flies in the air. It lands on Lily's head, on her mom's face, on the table, on the floor.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "I'm sorry, mom!"

Mom laughs. She wipes the sauce from her face. She picks up the spaghetti from the floor. She puts it in a bowl. She says, "It's okay, Lily. Accidents happen. But we have to clean up now."

Lily helps mom clean up. She throws away the spaghetti that is dirty. She washes her hands and face. She says, "Can I have some more spaghetti, please?"

Mom smiles. She gives Lily another plate of spaghetti. She says, "Yes, you can. But be careful this time. And don't forget to taste it. I made it with a new sauce. It's a little sour, but I think you'll like it."

Lily tastes the sauce. She makes a face. She says, "Yuck! It's too sour! I don't like it!"

Mom laughs again. She says, "Well, maybe you'll like it better next time. Or maybe we can try a different sauce. Do you want some cheese and meatballs instead?"

Lily nods. She says, "Yes, please. I love cheese and meatballs. They are yummy!"

Mom and Lily eat their cheese and meatballs. They enjoy their dinner. They are happy. They love each other. They love spaghetti. Even when it slips.

Sara and Tom are friends. They live on a farm with many animals. Sara likes to name the animals. She gives them funny names. Tom likes to help Sara.

One day, Sara and Tom see a big car. A man and a woman get out of the car. They look rich. They have nice clothes and shiny things. They walk to the farm.

"Hello, we are Mr. and Mrs. Smith. We want to buy your farm," the man says.

Sara and Tom are surprised. They love their farm. They do not want to sell it.

"Why do you want our farm?" Sara asks.

"Because we are rich. We have a lot of money. We want to build a big house and a pool here. We do not like animals. They are dirty and noisy," the woman says.

Sara and Tom are angry. They do not like the Smiths. They love their animals. They are not dirty and noisy. They are cute and friendly.

"No, you cannot buy our farm. This is our home. We are happy here. Go away!" Tom says.

The Smiths are annoyed. They do not like children. They think they are rude and silly.

"Fine, we will go. But we will come back. We will make you sell your farm. We always get what we want," the man says.

He and the woman get in their car and drive away.

Sara and Tom hug each other. They are glad they have each other. They are glad they have their farm. They are not rich, but they are happy. They go to feed the animals and give them more funny names.

Lily liked to polish her board with a soft cloth. She had a big board with many colors and shapes on it. She could draw and write on it with a special pen. She loved her board very much. It was a gift from her grandma, who said it was expensive and rare.

One day, Lily had a friend over to play. His name was Ben. Ben saw Lily's board and wanted to try it. He asked Lily if he could use it. Lily said yes, but she told him to be careful and gentle with it. She said it was her favorite toy and it was expensive and rare.

Ben nodded, but he did not listen. He took the pen and drew hard and fast on the board. He made big scribbles and lines. He did not care about the colors and shapes. He did not care about Lily's feelings. He just wanted to have fun.

Lily saw what Ben was doing and felt sad and angry. She ran to him and tried to stop him. She said, "Ben, stop! You are ruining my board! You are not careful and gentle! You are not a good friend!"

Ben looked at Lily and laughed. He said, "Lily, it's just a board! It's not expensive and rare! It's just a toy! You are silly and boring! You are not a good friend!"

Lily felt hurt and cried. She took her board and ran to her room. She locked the door and did not want to see Ben anymore. She tried to polish her board, but it was too late. The board was scratched and stained. It was not beautiful and fun anymore. It was broken and sad.

Moral: We should respect and care for other people's things, especially if they are expensive and rare. We should also respect and care for other people's feelings, especially if they are our friends. We should not be selfish and rude. We should be careful and gentle. We should be good friends.

Ben is sad and angry. He does not like to lose the ball or the game. He sits on the bench and watches Tom, Sam and Lily play. He sees them smile and applaud each other. He feels lonely and bored.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Playing together is better than playing alone. Saying sorry and thank you is polite and nice.

Anna waved at the zoom and said, "Hello, zoom! Can you help me? There is a cat on the tree and I want to save it!" The zoom stopped and a man came out. He was wearing a yellow hat and a black coat. He smiled at Anna and said, "Hello, little superhero! I am a firefighter. I can help you with the cat. Do you want to use my ladder?"

She petted the cat and said, "It's okay, cat. I am here to help you. You are safe now." She picked up the cat and carried it down the ladder. The cat purred and licked Anna's face.

Tom was a lawyer. He helped people who had problems. He liked his job, but sometimes it was hard. One day, he had to go to a big building with many rooms. He had to talk to a man who was angry and mean. The man wanted to take away Tom's client's house.

Tom was not scared of the man. He had many papers and facts to show that his client was right. He waited for his turn to speak in front of a judge. The judge was a fair and kind person who listened to both sides. Tom hoped the judge would help his client keep his house.

"Can we play with Rex?" Lily asked Dad.

"Sure, if you want to. He loves to play." Dad said.

Lily and Ben were happy. They forgot their fear. They played with Rex in the snow. They made a snowman and had a snowball fight. They had fun. They were not nervous or shivering anymore. They were warm and cozy.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play outside in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They also gave him two eyes and a mouth made of coal.

"Look at our snowman, he is so happy!" Sara said.

"Yes, he is. But I am cold and hungry. Can we go inside now?" Ben asked.

Sara nodded and they ran to their house. They saw their dog, Spot, waiting for them at the door. Spot was a big, fluffy dog who loved to cuddle with them.

"Hi, Spot! You are so warm and cozy!" Sara said, hugging him.

Ben was jealous of Sara and Spot. He wanted to hug Spot too, but Spot only had eyes for Sara.

"Spot, come here! I want to hug you too!" Ben said.

But Spot did not listen. He licked Sara's face and wagged his tail.

Ben felt sad and angry. He shivered in the cold and wished he had a friend like Spot.

He looked at the snowman and had an idea. He ran to the snowman and took the hat, the scarf and the coal from his face.

"Hey, what are you doing?" Sara shouted.

"I am making a friend for me. You have Spot, I have Snowy!" Ben said.

He put the hat, the scarf and the coal on a smaller snowball and made a face for it.

"See? This is Snowy. He is my friend. He likes me more than you!" Ben said.

Sara was shocked and hurt. She loved her brother and wanted to share Spot with him. She did not like that he took the things from their snowman.

"That is not nice, Ben. You ruined our snowman. And Snowy is not a real friend. He is just a snowball. He cannot hug you or talk to you or play with you!" Sara said.

Ben did not care. He hugged Snowy and pretended he was happy.

"Snowy is a real friend. He is better than Spot. He is not jealous of you. He is not warm and cozy, but he is cool and fun!" Ben said.

Sara felt sorry for Ben. She knew he was lonely and cold. She wanted to make him feel better.

She took Spot by the collar and walked to Ben and Snowy.

"Ben, I am sorry you are cold and hungry. I am too. Why don't we go inside and have some hot chocolate and cookies? We can share them with Spot and Snowy. They can be friends too!" Sara said.

Ben looked at Sara and Spot. He saw that they were not mean or selfish. They were kind and generous. He felt ashamed of what he did.

He let go of Snowy and smiled at Sara.

"OK, Sara. I am sorry I ruined our snowman. And I am sorry I was jealous of Spot. You are right, he is a good dog. And Snowy is not a real friend. He is just a snowball. Can we make a new snowman tomorrow?" Ben said.

Sara nodded and hugged Ben.

"Of course we can, Ben. I love you, brother. And I love Spot and Snowy too. Come on, let's go inside. It is too cold out here!" Sara said.

They took Spot and Snowy with them and went inside. They had hot chocolate and cookies and laughed and talked. They were happy and warm. They were a family.

Tom and Lily love to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the jet. The jet is big and red and makes a loud noise when they push a button. They like to pretend they are flying to faraway places.

One day, Tom and Lily are playing with the jet in the living room. Lily wants to fly the jet to the moon. She says, "Tom, can I have the jet? I want to go to the moon."

Tom says, "No, Lily, it is my turn. I want to go to the jungle."

Lily says, "But you had the jet for a long time. It is not fair. Please share the jet with me."

Tom says, "No, Lily, the jet is mine. Go away."

Lily feels sad and angry. She thinks Tom is selfish. She says, "Tom, you are selfish. You do not care about me. You are not a good brother."

Tom feels hurt and angry. He thinks Lily is selfish. He says, "Lily, you are selfish. You do not care about me. You are not a good sister."

They start to fight over the jet. They pull and tug and shout. The jet falls to the floor and breaks. They both cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the broken jet and the crying children. She says, "What happened here? Why are you fighting?"

Tom and Lily tell Mom what happened. They blame each other for being selfish. Mom says, "Tom and Lily, you are both selfish. You do not love each other. You do not share your toys. You do not respect your jet. You should be sorry."

Tom and Lily feel ashamed. They realize they were wrong. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We love each other. We love our jet. We will share our toys. We will respect our jet."

Mom says, "I am glad you are sorry. I love you both. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to fix your jet. And you have to play nicely together."

Tom and Lily hug Mom and say, "Thank you, Mom. We will fix our jet. We will play nicely together."

They take the jet to their room and try to fix it. They work together and help each other. They say, "We are sorry, jet. We love you, jet. We will take care of you, jet."

They fix the jet and make it fly again. They smile and hug each other. They say, "We are happy, jet. We love you, jet. We will share you, jet."

They fly the jet to the moon and the jungle and many other places. They have fun and laugh. They are not selfish anymore. They are good brother and sister.

Tim and Sam were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big box with a knob. When they turned the knob, the box made funny noises and showed them pictures of animals.

One night, they were playing with the box before bedtime. They saw a lion, a monkey, a giraffe, and a penguin. They laughed and tried to imitate the noises and the movements of the animals.

"Look, I'm a lion! Roar!" Tim said, and he made his face scary and his hair messy.

"I'm a monkey! Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!" Sam said, and he jumped on the bed and swung his arms.

They had so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them.

"Tim, Sam, it's time to sleep! Turn off the box and brush your teeth!" Mom said from the door.

But Tim and Sam did not want to stop playing. They pretended they did not hear Mom and turned the knob again.

This time, the box showed them a picture of an elderly man with a long beard and a hat. He looked very tired and bored. He did not make any noise, he just yawned.

"Who is that?" Tim asked, and he tilted his head.

"I don't know. He looks old and sleepy." Sam said, and he yawned too.

The box did not change the picture. It stayed on the elderly man, who yawned again and again.

Tim and Sam felt their eyes getting heavy. They yawned more and more. They could not play anymore. They were too sleepy.

"Maybe we should sleep too." Tim said, and he turned off the box.

"OK. Good night, Tim." Sam said, and he crawled into his bed.

"Good night, Sam." Tim said, and he did the same.

They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of lions and monkeys and giraffes and penguins. And they did not see the elderly man again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big yellow slide. They wanted to go on it.

"Let's go on the slide!" Tom said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They ran to the slide. But when they touched it, they felt something hot.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom cried. "The slide is hot!"

Lily let go of the slide. She looked at her hand. It was red.

"Are you OK?" she asked Tom.

Tom nodded. He looked at his hand. It was red too.

They heard a voice behind them.

"Hey, kids, be careful!" the voice said. "The slide is hot from the sun. You should not touch it. It can hurt you."

They turned around. They saw a man in a blue shirt. He was a park worker. He had a bucket of water and a cloth.

He came to them. He smiled. He dipped the cloth in the water. He gently wiped their hands.

"That's better," he said. "The water will cool your hands. You should always warn each other before you touch something hot. And you should always listen to warnings from grown-ups. They know what is safe and what is not."

"Thank you, sir," Lily and Tom said.

"You're welcome, kids," the man said. "Now, why don't you go and play on the swings? They are not hot. They are fun."

Lily and Tom nodded. They thanked the man again. They ran to the swings. They had fun. They learned to warn each other and to listen to warnings. They did not touch anything hot again.

Tom is amazed. He wants to grow a sunflower too. "Can I have a seed?" he asks.

Lila smiles. She has more seeds in her pocket. She gives one to Tom. "Here you go," she says. "You can plant it in your garden. Then you can have a sunflower too!"

Lily is a smart kid. She likes to ride her bike. She can ride fast and slow. She can ride on the road and on the grass. She can ride with one hand and with no hands.

One day, Lily sees a big hill. She wants to ride up the hill. She pedals hard and hard. She feels strong and happy. She gets to the top of the hill. She sees a lot of trees and flowers. She sees a lake and a boat. She sees a bird and a cloud. She smiles and says, "Wow!"

Lily was a little bunny who loved to hop. She hopped in the grass, in the garden, and in the forest. She always carried a bag with her, where she kept her favorite things: a carrot, a book, and a toy.

One day, she met a big bear who was very hungry. The bear saw Lily's bag and wanted to take it. He said, "Give me your bag, little bunny, or I will eat you!"

Lily was scared, but she did not want to lose her bag. She said, "No, this is my bag, and these are my things. You cannot have them, big bear!"

The bear growled and chased Lily. Lily hopped as fast as she could, but the bear was faster. He caught up with her and grabbed her bag. He opened it and saw the carrot, the book, and the toy. He said, "What is this? This is not food, this is rubbish!"

He threw the bag away and left. Lily was sad and cried. She lost her bag and her things. She wished she had shared with the bear, maybe he would have been nice to her.

Then, she heard a voice. It was a squirrel who had seen everything. He said, "Don't cry, little bunny, I have your bag. The bear did not want it, so I took it. Here, you can have it back."

Lily was happy and thanked the squirrel. She said, "You are very kind, squirrel. Do you want to share my carrot, my book, and my toy with me?"

The squirrel smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to. Sharing is fun, and it makes friends."

Lily and the squirrel sat down and shared. They ate the carrot, read the book, and played with the toy. They had a peaceful and happy time. They learned that sharing is better than being greedy, and that kindness is better than being mean.

Lila and Ben were best friends. They liked to play outside and explore new places. One day, they found a swamp near their house. It was wet and muddy and full of strange plants and animals.

"Look, Ben, a frog!" Lila said, pointing to a green creature that jumped into the water.

"Wow, can we catch it?" Ben asked, excited.

They ran after the frog, but it was too fast and clever. It hid under a big leaf and croaked. Lila and Ben laughed and decided to skip around the swamp. They skipped over rocks and logs and puddles. They felt happy and free.

But then, they saw something incredible. It was a big, shiny, purple flower. It smelled sweet and had a long stem. Lila and Ben had never seen anything like it before.

"Ben, look, a magic flower!" Lila said, amazed.

"Let's pick it and take it home!" Ben said, reaching for it.

But as soon as he touched the flower, it snapped. It was not a flower at all, but a trap. It was a hungry plant that ate bugs and frogs and sometimes bigger things. It closed its mouth around Ben's hand and tried to pull him in.

"Help, Lila, help!" Ben screamed.

Lila was scared, but she was brave. She grabbed a stick and hit the plant hard. She hit it again and again, until it let go of Ben. Ben pulled his hand out and hugged Lila.

"Thank you, Lila, you saved me!" Ben said, grateful.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Lila asked, worried.

"I'm okay, just a little hurt. Let's go home, Lila. I don't like this swamp anymore." Ben said, shaking.

"Me neither, Ben. Let's go home and tell mom and dad what happened. Maybe they will give us a cookie and a band-aid." Lila said, holding Ben's hand.

They ran away from the swamp, leaving the plant behind. They learned a lesson that day: not everything that looks pretty is nice. And they were glad they had each other.

The dog does not like Sam. The dog growls and snaps at Sam. Sam is surprised and scared. He tries to run away, but the dog is faster. The dog bites Sam's leg and makes him fall. Sam cries and says, "Help, help!"

Ben hears Sam's cry. He feels bad for Sam. He wants to help Sam. He sees a stick on the ground. He picks up the stick and runs to the dog. He hits the dog with the stick and says, "Go away, dog. Leave Sam alone!"

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that it is important to be brave and help your friends when they are in trouble, but also to be smart and avoid danger when you don't know what is safe.

But Tom is mean. He does not like Sara. He wants to make her sad. He says, "Sara does not know. She is dumb. She is a baby." He laughs at her. The other kids laugh too. Sara feels bad. She lowers her hand. She does not answer.

The teacher sees Sara. She is sad. She asks her, "Sara, do you know the answer?" Sara nods. She whispers, "Giraffe." The teacher smiles. She says, "That is right, Sara. You are smart. You are not a baby. You are a big girl." She gives her a sticker. Sara feels happy. She thanks the teacher.

But Tom is angry. He does not get a sticker. He does not like Sara. He wants to hurt her. He waits for recess. He follows Sara outside. He pushes her down. He takes her sticker. He says, "This is mine. You do not deserve it. You are a baby. You are dumb." He runs away. Sara cries. She is hurt. She is cold.

You need to say sorry. You need to give back the sticker. You need to go to time out." She takes Tom to the corner. She makes him sit. She says, "You need to learn to be kind. The moral of the story is: Be kind to others. Do not be mean. Respect others. Share. Be a good friend.

Ben and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Sometimes they found big shells that had something inside. Mom and Dad said those were oysters. Oysters were animals that lived in the water and made pearls.

One day, Ben and Lily found a very big oyster shell. They opened it and saw a shiny white ball. It was a pearl. They were very happy and showed it to Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad smiled and said they were very lucky. They said a pearl was a rare and beautiful thing that oysters made.

Ben and Lily wanted to know how oysters made pearls. Mom and Dad tried to explain. They said oysters had soft bodies that they protected with their shells. Sometimes, a small thing, like a grain of sand, got inside the shell and hurt the oyster. The oyster covered the thing with a smooth layer of something called nacre. The oyster did this over and over until the thing became a pearl.

Ben and Lily listened and nodded. They thought oysters were very clever and gifted. They thanked the oyster for giving them the pearl. They decided to keep the pearl as a special treasure and a reminder of their fun day at the beach.

Tim was lonely. He had no friends to play with. He lived in a big house with his mom and dad, but they were always busy. He wished he had a pet, like a dog or a cat, to keep him company.

One day, he found a jug in the garage. It was old and dusty, but it had a funny shape. It looked like a fat man with a big nose and a hat. Tim liked the jug. He took it to his room and cleaned it with a cloth. He put it on his shelf and said, "Hello, jug. You are my friend now. What is your name?"

The jug did not answer. Tim was sad. He thought the jug did not like him. He went to bed and hugged his pillow.

The next morning, he heard a strange noise. It sounded like a sneeze. He opened his eyes and saw the jug on his shelf. It was moving and shaking. It had a face and a mouth. It said, "Achoo! Achoo! Excuse me, I have a cold. I'm sorry, I did not talk to you yesterday. I was asleep. I'm a magic jug. My name is Juggy. And you are?"

Tim was surprised and happy. He jumped out of bed and ran to the jug. He said, "Wow, you can talk! You are a magic jug! My name is Tim. I'm glad you are awake. You are my friend, right?"

Juggy smiled and nodded. He said, "Yes, I'm your friend. And you are mine. I was lonely too, in the garage. I'm happy you found me. We can have fun together. Do you want to play a game?"

Tim nodded and clapped his hands. He said, "Yes, I want to play a game. What game do you want to play?"

Juggy thought for a moment. He said, "How about hide and seek? I'll hide first. You count to ten and then look for me. Ready, set, go!"

Juggy jumped off the shelf and rolled under the bed. Tim covered his eyes and counted to ten. Then he opened his eyes and looked for Juggy. He searched the room, but he could not find him. He heard a giggle from under the bed. He bent down and saw Juggy's nose sticking out. He said, "I found you, Juggy! You are a good hider. Now it's my turn to hide. You count to ten and then look for me."

Juggy agreed and covered his eyes. He counted to ten and then opened his eyes. He looked for Tim, but he could not see him. He heard a laugh from behind the curtain. He rolled to the window and pulled the curtain. He saw Tim hiding behind it. He said, "I found you, Tim! You are a good hider too. You are a smart boy. I like you."

Tim and Juggy hugged and laughed. They played more games and told each other stories. They had a lot of fun. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy. They were friends.

"Hello, I am Mimi the mole. Who are you?" the mole says.

Ben and Sam are surprised. They have never seen a mole before. They have never heard a mole talk before.

"We are Ben and Sam. We are kids. We play in the park. What are you doing here?" Ben says.

"I live here. This is my home. I dig tunnels and eat worms. That is normal for moles. What do you do?" Mimi says.

"We run and jump and swing and slide. We eat sandwiches and cookies. That is normal for kids. Do you want to play with us?" Sam says.

Mimi thinks for a moment. She likes Ben and Sam. They are nice and curious. But she also likes her home and her worms. She does not want to leave them.

"Thank you, but no. I have to stay here. This is where I belong. But you can come and visit me anytime. I like to make new friends." Mimi says.

Ben and Sam understand. They say goodbye to Mimi. They promise to come back soon. They go back to their games. They are happy. They have met a mole. A mole that can talk. That is not normal. But that is okay. They like Mimi. She is their friend.

Lily and Tom looked around. Miss Rose was not in the room. She had gone to the office for a minute. Lily had an idea.

"Let's steal some crayons," she whispered. "We can hide them in our pockets and take them home. Then we can draw anything we want."

Tom was scared. He knew stealing was bad. But he also wanted to use the brilliant crayons. He nodded his head.

The moral of the story is: Don't quit something you love because you think you are not good enough. Practice and have fun. Be yourself and enjoy your own style and pace. You are a beautiful dancer.

One day, when mom was not home, Anna opened the drawer and took out a pretty necklace. It had many colors and sparkles. Anna put it around her neck and smiled. She wanted to show it to her teddy bear.

But as she walked to her room, the necklace got caught on the door handle. Anna pulled hard, but the necklace did not come off. She pulled harder, and the necklace broke. The beads and the string separated and fell on the floor.

Anna was scared and sad. She did not want to break mom's pretty necklace. She did not know what to do. She picked up the beads and the string and ran to her room. She hid them under her bed and hoped mom would not find out.

But mom did find out. She saw the beads and the string under Anna's bed when she came home. She was angry and upset. She went to Anna and asked her what happened.

"Anna, did you take my necklace from the drawer?" mom asked.

Anna nodded. She was sorry. She did not mean to break it.

"Why did you take it, Anna? You know you are not supposed to touch my things without asking." mom said.

"I wanted to play with it. It was so pretty. I wanted to be a princess." Anna said.

"I understand, Anna, but you have to be careful with other people's things. They are not toys. They can break or get lost. And they can have special meanings. This necklace was a gift from your grandma. She gave it to me before she died. It was very important to me." mom said.

Anna felt bad. She did not know the necklace was from grandma. She loved grandma. She missed her.

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I love you and grandma. Can you fix the necklace?" Anna asked.

Mom hugged Anna. She was not angry anymore. She was sad, but she also loved Anna.

"I love you too, Anna. And I miss grandma too. I don't know if I can fix the necklace, but I will try. Maybe we can do it together. And next time, if you want to play with my things, you have to ask me first. OK?" mom said.

"OK, mom. Thank you. Can I help you?" Anna said.

"Yes, you can. Come on, let's go to the drawer and see what we can do." mom said.

They went to the drawer and picked up the beads and the string. They tried to put them back together. It was hard, but it was also fun. They talked about grandma and her pretty things. They smiled and laughed. They felt closer. They did not separate.

Her dad says, "Sure, Lily. We can come back tomorrow. I'm proud of you. You learned something new today. You are a good hockey player." He gives her a high five. They go home happy.

"Go away, dog!" Ben says. He throws a stick at the dog. The dog runs after the stick. Ben and Sara run away too. They hide behind a tree.

"Are you okay, Sara?" Ben asks. He sees that Sara is crying. Her knee is red and has a small cut. She fell when she ran from the dog.

"I'm okay, Ben. But my knee hurts. And the dog was scary." Sara says. She wipes her tears with her hand.

"I have an idea, Sara. Let's go to my house. My mom can help your knee. And she can give us cookies and milk. And we can play with my toys. Do you want to come?" Ben says. He smiles at Sara.

"Yes, Ben. I want to come. Thank you for being my friend." Sara says. She smiles back at Ben. She stands up and holds his hand. They walk to his house.

Before they leave the park, they see the dog again. The dog is not barking now. He is lying on the grass. He looks weak and sad. He has no stick and no friends.

"Maybe the dog is not bad, Ben. Maybe he is lonely and wants to play." Sara says. She feels sorry for the dog.

"Maybe you are right, Sara. Maybe we can be his friends too." Ben says. He feels brave and kind.

They go to the dog. They talk to him in a soft voice. They pet his fur. They give him some of their cookies. The dog wags his tail. He licks their faces. He is happy.

Sara and Ben hug the dog. They hug each other. They are happy too. They have a new friend.

As they played, their cars went faster and faster. Suddenly, Tim's car got stuck in the mud. Sam stopped his car and said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you." Sam pulled Tim's car out of the mud, and they continued to play. They had so much fun driving their cars and became good friends.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little bunny named Ben. Ben loved to hop and play all day. One day, while playing, Ben saw an amazing hole under a big tree. Ben was very curious and wanted to see what was inside the hole.

Ben hopped closer to the hole and peeked inside. It was very dark, and he couldn't see anything. Just then, he heard a small yawn coming from the hole. Ben wondered who could be inside. He called out, "Hello! Who is in there?"

A tiny mouse named Molly came out of the hole, rubbing her eyes. She had been taking a nap inside her cozy home. Molly and Ben became good friends. They played together and had lots of fun every day. The amazing hole under the tree became their favorite place to meet and play.

The rabbit opened his eyes and began to look for his friends. He found the squirrel hidden in a tree. Then, he found the bird under a bush. But he could not find the turtle.

The rabbit and his friends looked everywhere for the turtle. They were getting worried. Then, the rabbit remembered a big rock he had seen when he was counting. They went to the rock, and there was the turtle, hidden behind it! The turtle had won the game.

The group of friends laughed and clapped for the turtle. They were happy they had found him. They played more games and had a great day together.

"It's ugly and I don't like it," Lily said.

"But it's good for you," her mom said. 

Lily didn't listen and pushed the broccoli away. Later that night, Lily's mom was cooking something on the stove and accidentally left the burner on. The pot started to burn and smoke filled the kitchen. 

"Mommy, something is burning!" Lily yelled.

Her mom quickly turned off the burner and opened the windows to let the smoke out. 

"Thank you for telling me, Lily. You saved us from a big problem," her mom said. 

From that day on, Lily always ate her broccoli and listened to her mom's advice.

Finally, the farmer went to the chicken and said, "Cluck, are you hungry?" The chicken replied, "Cluck, yes please!" The farmer then gave the chicken some corn to eat. 

All of the animals were happy and full because the farmer was so organized and took good care of them. The end.

"Wow, Tom, it is so round and so tight!" Sue says.

"Can I have it?" Tom asks.

"No, I want it!" Sue says.

They both grab the ball and pull it. They pull it very hard. They pull it so hard that the ball pops. It makes a loud noise. Tom and Sue are scared. They drop the ball. The ball is not round and tight anymore. It is flat and soft.

"Oh no, Tom, we broke the ball!" Sue says.

"Oh no, Sue, we did!" Tom says.

They feel sad. They look at the ball. They see a tag on the ball. The tag says: "This is not a ball. This is a balloon. Do not pull it. It will pop."

Tom and Sue learn a new word. They learn what a balloon is. They also learn to be careful with new things. They say sorry to the balloon. They go to find another ball to play with. They are still friends.

One day, Mom comes to their room. She is not happy. She says, "Sara and Ben, you need to clean your room. It is too messy. You have to put your toys, books, and clothes in their places. If you do that, I will supply you with a treat. Do you promise?"

They decide to make a plan. They wait for the boy to go down the slide. Then they run to the top of the slide. They seat on the slide together. They say, "Now it is our turn. You are not welcome here." They slide down fast.

But the slide is broken. There is a hole in the middle of the slide. Anna and Ben fall through the hole. They land on the ground. They hurt their legs and arms. They cry. The boy laughs. He says, "That is what you get for being rude. You are terrible." He goes on the slide again.

Anna and Ben are hurt and sad. They wish they had not gone on the slide. They wish they had been nice to the boy. They wish they had found another game to play. They learn a hard lesson. The end.

Lila and Ben were playing with paper. They liked to fold the paper and make different shapes. Lila made a hat, and Ben made a boat.

"Look, I made a hat!" Lila said, putting it on her head. "Do you like it?"

"Yes, it is very nice," Ben said. "But look, I made a boat! It can float on the water. Do you want to try?"

Lila nodded, and they ran to the pond. They put the boat on the water and watched it sail. They were very happy.

But then, a goose came. The goose saw the boat and thought it was food. It swam to the boat and bit it. The boat sank in the water.

"Oh no!" Lila and Ben cried. "The goose ate our boat!"

The goose honked and flapped its wings. It did not care about the boat. It was hungry and wanted more food.

"That is not fair!" Lila said. "The goose is mean. It should not eat our boat. We worked hard to make it."

Ben agreed. He was sad and angry. He picked up a stick and threw it at the goose. The stick hit the goose on the head.

"Ouch!" the goose said. "That hurts! Why did you do that?"

"Because you ate our boat!" Ben said. "That was not nice. You should say sorry."

The goose felt sorry. It realized it had done something wrong. It swam to the shore and looked at Lila and Ben.

"I am sorry," the goose said. "I did not know it was your boat. I thought it was food. I was hungry and did not see well. Can you forgive me?"

Lila and Ben looked at the goose. They saw that it was sorry. They decided to forgive it.

"It is okay," Lila said. "We forgive you. But next time, please do not eat our things. We can share with you if you ask nicely."

"Yes, we can be friends," Ben said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The goose nodded. It was happy. It wanted to play with Lila and Ben. They gave it some bread and some paper. They taught it how to fold the paper and make different shapes. They had fun together. They learned to be kind and fair.

"Good try, Lily. But you have to make your loop smaller, and your knot looser. Then your shoes will stay on," Anna said.

Lily tried again. She made a smaller loop, a better cross, and a looser knot. She looked at her shoes. They looked like Anna's shoes. She smiled.

"Did I do it right?" Lily asked.

Ben and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans. They also liked to hide in the cupboard under the sink. It was dark and cozy and they could hear their mom and dad talking in the living room.

"Can I go in the cupboard first?" Lily asked Ben.

"Okay, but only for a little bit. Then it's my turn," Ben said.

Lily crawled into the cupboard and closed the door behind her. She felt around for a soft towel to sit on. She found one and smiled. She liked the cupboard. It was like her own secret place.

Ben waited outside the cupboard. He counted to ten slowly. Then he knocked on the door.

"Lily, are you done? Can I go in now?" he asked.

No answer.

"Lily, can you hear me? It's my turn," he said louder.

Still no answer.

Ben started to worry. Maybe Lily was asleep. Maybe she was sick. Maybe she was stuck. He tried to open the door, but it was locked. He pushed and pulled, but it did not move.

He started to cry.

"Mom! Dad! Help! Lily is in the cupboard and I can't open it!" he shouted.

Mom and dad heard Ben's cry and ran to the kitchen. They saw him crying by the cupboard. They saw the lock on the door.

"What happened, Ben? Why is Lily in the cupboard?" mom asked.

"We were playing and she went in and she did not come out and I can't open it and I'm sorry and please help her!" Ben sobbed.

Dad took a key from his pocket and unlocked the door. He opened it and saw Lily inside. She was awake, but very quiet.

"Lily, are you okay? Why didn't you answer Ben?" dad asked.

Lily looked at dad with big eyes. She pointed to her mouth. She had a big spoonful of peanut butter in it. She had found a jar of peanut butter in the cupboard and decided to eat some. But it was too sticky and she could not talk.

"I'm sorry, dad. I was hungry and I found peanut butter and I ate some and it was yummy but it was sticky and I could not talk and I did not hear Ben and I'm sorry," she said after she swallowed.

Mom and dad looked at each other and smiled. They hugged Lily and Ben and helped them out of the cupboard.

"It's okay, Lily. We're glad you're okay. But next time, please don't eat peanut butter in the cupboard. It's not good for you and it's uncomfortable. And please answer Ben when he calls you. He was very worried about you," mom said.

"And next time, please don't lock the cupboard. It's not safe and it's scary. And please share the cupboard with Ben. He likes it too," dad said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They promised to play nicely and not lock the cupboard again.

Mom and dad smiled and kissed them. They gave them some milk and cookies and told them they loved them.

They all sat down at the table and ate and talked and laughed. They were happy.

Lily liked to sort things. She sorted her toys by color, her books by size, and her clothes by pattern. She also liked to sort things in the kitchen, when her mom let her help. She sorted the spoons, the cups, and the plates. But her favorite thing to sort was the pastry.

Every Saturday, her mom made pastry for breakfast. She made croissants, muffins, and scones. She put them in a big basket and covered them with a cloth. Lily loved to peek under the cloth and sort the pastry by shape. She made a pile of croissants, a pile of muffins, and a pile of scones. She counted them and smelled them and sometimes tasted them.

One day, her mom had a surprise for her. She said, "Lily, today I made a special pastry for you. It's in the basket, but you have to wait until breakfast to see it. Can you do that?" Lily nodded, but she was very curious. She wondered what the special pastry was. Was it round or square? Was it sweet or salty? Was it big or small?

She waited for a while, but she could not stop thinking about the pastry. She decided to take a quick look. She tiptoed to the basket and lifted the cloth. She saw the croissants, the muffins, and the scones. But she also saw something else. It was a pastry she had never seen before. It was shaped like a star, and it had sprinkles on top. It looked very yummy.

She reached out to touch it, but before she could, she heard a voice. It was her mom. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? I told you to wait until breakfast. You are very nosy, aren't you?" Lily felt ashamed. She dropped the cloth and ran to her mom. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to see the special pastry. It's very pretty. Can I have it, please?" Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Of course you can, Lily. But first, you have to sort the pastry again. You messed up the piles. Can you do that?" Lily nodded and ran back to the basket. She sorted the pastry by shape again. She made sure to put the star pastry on top. She was happy. She learned a lesson. She would not be nosy again. She would wait for surprises.

Sam is sad. He follows Jen. He wants to stop her. He wants to give the phone back.

But Jen is fast. She runs to the other side of the park. She finds a slide. She climbs up the slide. She holds the phone in her hand.

She smiles. She thinks she is smart. She thinks she is brave. She thinks she is independent.

He tries to help Jen. He tries to call for help. But the phone does not work. It is broken. He does not know what to do.

He wishes he had his own phone. He wishes Jen had listened to him. He wishes they had not played with the phone.

He learns a hard lesson. He learns that trust is important. He learns that independent is not always good. He learns that bad things can happen.

She had an idea. She found a big rock, and she rub it against the pond. It made lots of bubbles! She was so happy, she started splashing even more, and the bubbles followed behind her. 

The duck had lots of fun splashing around with her bubble friends all day. She felt better already! 

The end.

Then, an elderly lady came along. She noticed Tommy looking frightened and asked why. Tommy pointed at the man with the saw and the elderly lady smiled.

She explained to Tommy that the elderly man was going to use the saw to build something in the park. He was going to make a beautiful wooden bench where everyone could sit.

Tommy couldn't believe it. He was happy to hear it and smiled. He thanked the elderly lady and eagerly watched the elderly man create his masterpiece.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play chess with his grandpa. Timmy's grandpa was very good at chess, and Timmy always lost. One day, Timmy asked his grandpa, "Why do I always lose?" His grandpa replied, "Because you don't practice enough, my dear."

But then, a kind lady found Timmy's backpack and gave it back to him. Timmy was happy and thanked the lady. The lady told Timmy that she was very wealthy and didn't need anything in return. She just wanted to help him. Timmy felt grateful and wanted to give the lady a hug. He asked his mom if he could release himself from her hand and go hug the lady. His mom said yes and Timmy ran to give the lady a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to run and hop around in the wild fields. One day, Benny saw a big carrot patch and he hoped he could win one for himself. So, he hopped over to the patch and started nibbling on the carrots.

But, suddenly, Benny heard a loud noise and saw a big, scary fox running towards him. Benny tried to hop away, but the fox was too fast. The fox caught Benny and sadly, Benny didn't win the carrot he hoped for. 

The moral of the story is that sometimes we may not win what we hope for, but it's important to stay safe and be careful in the wild.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and saw a big shadow coming towards him. It was one of the foolish birds! The little bug tried to crawl away as fast as he could, but it was too late. Tim and Anna were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a new boy sitting on a bench. He looked sad and lonely. He had big sunglasses on his eyes.

"Who is he?" Tim asked Anna.

"I don't know. Maybe we can introduce ourselves and be nice to him," Anna said.

They walked over to the bench and smiled at the boy.

"Hi, we are Tim and Anna. What is your name?" Anna asked.

The boy did not answer. He looked down and fiddled with his sunglasses.

"Are you shy? Do you want to play with us?" Tim asked.

The boy shook his head. He whispered, "No, thank you. I can't play. I can't see very well. My sunglasses help me a little, but not much. I feel helpless."

Tim and Anna felt sorry for the boy. They wanted to help him.

"That's okay. You don't have to play if you don't want to. But we can still be your friends. We can talk to you and listen to you. Maybe we can find something fun to do together that doesn't need good eyes," Anna said.

The boy looked up and smiled a little. He said, "Really? You would do that for me?"

"Of course. We are nice and friendly. We like to make new friends. What is your name?" Tim said.

The boy said, "My name is Leo. Thank you for being kind to me. You make me feel less helpless."

Tim and Anna hugged Leo and said, "You're welcome. We are happy to meet you. Let's be friends."

The moral of the story is: Be kind and friendly to people who are different from you. You can make them feel less helpless and more happy. You can also learn from them and have fun with them.

But it was too late. They were stuck in the water. They were running out of air. They were going to die.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They saw a big machine near the fence. It had wheels, buttons and lights. They wanted to see what it did.

"Let's go and look at the machine," Tom said.

"OK, but be careful. It might be naughty," Lily said.

They ran to the machine and climbed on it. They pushed the buttons and turned the wheels. The machine made noises and moved. They laughed and had fun.

But then, the machine started to go faster and faster. It went out of the garden and onto the road. Lily and Tom were scared. They wanted to get off, but they could not. They were stuck.

"Help! Help!" they shouted.

A man saw them and ran to the machine. He pressed a big red button and the machine stopped. He opened a door and helped Lily and Tom out.

"Are you OK?" he asked.

"Yes, thank you," Lily and Tom said.

"What were you doing on my machine?" the man asked. "This is not a toy. This is a tractor. It is for working on the farm. You could have been hurt."

"We are sorry," Lily and Tom said. "We were just playing. We did not know it was a tractor. We thought it was a machine."

"Well, you should not play with things that do not belong to you. And you should not go near the road. It is dangerous. Where are your parents?" the man asked.

"They are in the house. We will go back now," Lily and Tom said.

Max felt sad and angry. He did not like Lily's words. He said to her, "My collar may not be shiny, but it is special to me. It was a gift from my family who loves me very much. Your collar may be pretty, but it does not make you kind. You are rude and mean."

Lily did not care. She laughed and walked away. She did not want to be friends with Max. She only wanted to shine.

But as she walked, she did not see a hole in the ground. She fell into it and hurt her leg. She cried and cried, but no one came to help her. She wished she had a friend.

Then she heard a bark. It was Max. He had followed her and saw her fall. He ran to the hole and tried to pull her out. He said to her, "Are you okay, Lily? I am sorry you are hurt. I will help you."

Lily was surprised and grateful. She said to him, "Thank you, Max. You are very kind and brave. I am sorry I was rude and mean. Your collar is special and impressive. You are a good friend."

Max smiled and said, "You are welcome, Lily. I am glad you are okay. Your collar is shiny and pretty, but it is not as important as your heart. You can be a good friend too."

They hugged and became friends. They learned that shining is not only about how you look, but how you act. They learned to be kind and respectful to others. They learned that friendship is more valuable than stones.

Lily and Pepper were so happy. They hugged and thanked the leaf for helping them. Then, they went back home to tell mom and dad about their big adventure. From that day on, they always played carefully and remembered their special day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Dizzy. Dizzy had four soft paws. One day, Dizzy went for a walk and found a big ball. Dizzy loved to play with the ball. He would push it with his paws and chase it around.

But one day, another dog came to play. This dog was big and had a loud bark. The big dog said, "This ball belongs to me!" Dizzy was sad and didn't know what to do. He wanted to play with the ball, but the big dog wouldn't let him.

Dizzy thought and thought. Then, he had an idea. He said to the big dog, "Let's share the ball and play together!" The big dog liked this idea. So, Dizzy and the big dog played with the ball and became friends. They both had fun, and their paws got very tired. From that day on, they always played together and shared their toys.

Tim was shocked. He did not know that cats could talk. He thought about it and said, "Okay, we can play together." From that day on, Tim and the persistent cat played together in the backyard. They became best friends and had lots of fun.

Lily and Ben wanted to play outside in the snow. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They ran to the door and asked their mom if they could go.

"Wait a minute, children," their mom said. "It is very cold and windy today. The snow is dangerous. It can make you fall or hurt you. You have to be careful."

Lily and Ben nodded. They promised to be careful and not go far. Their mom let them go, but told them to come back soon.

Lily and Ben had fun in the snow. They made a snowman, threw snowballs and slid on the ice. They laughed and shouted with joy.

But then they saw a big hill covered with snow. It looked like a fun place to slide down. Lily wanted to try it. She ran to the hill and climbed up.

"Come on, Ben, let's slide down the hill!" she called to her brother.

Ben looked at the hill. He saw that it was very steep and slippery. He saw that there were rocks and trees at the bottom. He felt scared.

"No, Lily, I don't want to slide down the hill," he said. "It is too dangerous. We might get hurt. Let's go back to the snowman."

Lily refused to listen to Ben. She thought he was being silly and scared. She wanted to have more fun. She sat on the snow and pushed herself down the hill.

"Yay, this is fun!" she shouted as she slid down.

But then she saw that she was going too fast. She saw that she could not stop. She saw that she was heading towards the rocks and trees. She felt afraid.

"Help, help!" she screamed as she slid down.

Ben heard Lily scream. He ran to the hill and saw her slide down. He saw that she was in trouble. He wanted to help her.

He grabbed a big stick and ran after her. He reached the bottom of the hill and threw the stick in front of Lily. The stick hit the snow and made a bump. Lily hit the bump and flew off the snow. She landed on the soft grass, away from the rocks and trees.

She was safe, but she was hurt. She had a cut on her leg and a bruise on her arm. She cried and cried.

Ben ran to Lily and hugged her. He said he was sorry and he was glad she was okay. He said they should go back to their mom and get some help.

Lily nodded. She said she was sorry and she was stupid. She said she should have listened to Ben and not slide down the hill. She said she learned her lesson.

They walked back to their mom, holding hands. Their mom saw them and ran to them. She saw that Lily was hurt and she was worried. She asked them what happened and how they were.

Lily and Ben told their mom what happened. They said they were sorry and they were wrong. They said they would not play in the dangerous snow again.

Their mom hugged them and kissed them. She said she was proud of them for being brave and honest. She said she would take care of them and make them feel better.

She took them inside and gave them some hot chocolate and cookies. She cleaned Lily's cut and put a bandage on it. She rubbed Lily's bruise and put some ice on it. She read them a story and tucked them in bed.

Lily and Ben felt warm and cozy. They thanked their mom and said they loved her. They said they loved each other too. They fell asleep, dreaming of snow.

"Where did you get this doll?" Mama asks.

Tom and Lily liked to play by the harbor. They saw big boats and small boats and fish and birds. Sometimes they threw stones in the water and watched the ripples. They had fun.

One day, they saw a big boat with a red flag. It looked different from the other boats. They wanted to see it closer. They walked along the harbor until they reached the boat. They saw a rope ladder hanging from the side of the boat. They looked at each other and smiled.

They climbed the rope ladder and got on the boat. They saw many things on the boat. They saw barrels and boxes and nets and ropes. They saw a wheel and a bell and a flag. They saw a man sleeping on a hammock. They did not see anyone else.

They decided to explore the boat. They went to the front of the boat and saw a big cannon. They went to the back of the boat and saw a small cabin. They opened the door and saw a map and a chest and a parrot. The parrot said "Hello!" and they laughed.

They did not notice that the boat was moving. The wind blew the sail and the boat left the harbor. The boat went faster and faster and soon the land was far away. They looked around and saw only water and sky. They were scared.

They ran to the rope ladder but it was gone. It had fallen into the water. They shouted for help but no one heard them. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had not climbed the boat. They wished they were back on the land.

The man on the hammock woke up. He heard the children crying. He got up and saw them. He was angry. He asked them who they were and what they were doing on his boat. They told him they were sorry and they wanted to go home. He said they were stowaways and he would make them walk the plank.

He grabbed them and dragged them to the side of the boat. He pointed to the water and said "Jump!" They were terrified. They begged him to let them go. He said "No!" and pushed them.

They closed their eyes and felt the air and then the water. They splashed and sank and then rose again. They opened their eyes and saw the boat sailing away. They saw the man laughing and the parrot squawking. They saw the rope ladder floating near them. They were surprised.

They swam to the rope ladder and grabbed it. They pulled themselves up and climbed back on the boat. They saw the man and the parrot looking at them. They were shocked. They said "We vanished but we came back!" The man and the parrot said "What?" They were confused.

Tom and Lily ran to the wheel and turned it. They made the boat go back to the harbor. They saw the land and the people and the other boats. They were glad. They jumped off the boat and ran to their parents. They hugged them and told them what happened. They said they were sorry and they would never climb a strange boat again. They said they learned their lesson. They said they loved them. Their parents said they loved them too. They said they were glad they were safe. They said they were proud of them. They said they were brave. They said they were lucky. They said they were happy. They all smiled. The end.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toy rockets in the backyard. They liked to pretend they were astronauts and explore the stars. Lila had a red rocket and Ben had a blue one. They made zooming noises and flew their rockets around.

"Look, Lila, I found a new planet!" Ben said, pointing to a big ball of dirt in the corner. "It's brown and round and has rocks on it. Let's land there and see what's inside."

"Yuck, Ben, put that down. It's gross," Lila said, making a face. "Let's go back to our rockets. I don't like this planet."

"Fine, Lila, but I want to take this worm with me. Maybe it can be my pet," Ben said, putting the worm in his pocket. He ran back to his rocket and got in. Lila followed him.

But as they were about to take off, they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a big dog running towards them. It was their neighbor's dog, Rex. He had escaped from his yard and smelled the dirt ball. He thought it was a toy and wanted to play with it.

"Uh-oh, Lila, we have a problem," Ben said, looking scared. "Rex is coming and he's going to destroy our planet!"

"Quick, Ben, let's go!" Lila said, pushing a button on her rocket. Her rocket flew up in the air and away from Rex. But Ben's rocket was stuck. The worm had crawled out of his pocket and into the engine. It had jammed the wires and made the rocket stop working.

"Help, Lila, help!" Ben shouted, trying to fix his rocket. But it was too late. Rex reached the dirt ball and bit into it. He shook his head and tossed the dirt ball in the air. It broke into pieces and fell to the ground. Ben's rocket was smashed and buried under the dirt.

Lila saw what happened and gasped. She flew back to Ben and landed next to him. She got out of her rocket and hugged him.

"Ben, are you OK?" she asked, worried.

"I'm sorry, Ben. That was a bad dog. He shouldn't have done that," Lila said, comforting him.

"Maybe, Ben. But for now, let's go inside and have some cookies. And tell Mom what happened. She'll make us feel better," Lila said, taking his hand.

"OK, Lila. That sounds fine," Ben said, smiling a little.

They left their rockets and the dirt ball behind and went inside. Rex followed them and wagged his tail. He didn't know he had done anything wrong. He just wanted to have fun.

One day, she saw a boy at the park. He had a ball and a bike. He looked at Lily's wagon and smiled. He asked her if he could play with it. Lily said no. She said it was her wagon and she did not want to share.

The boy was sad. He said he just wanted to try it for a little while. He said he would let her play with his ball and his bike. Lily said no again. She said she did not care about his ball and his bike. She said she only liked her wagon.

The boy was angry. He said Lily was spoiled and mean. He said he would take her wagon anyway. He ran to her wagon and tried to pull it away. Lily screamed and held on to it. They both pulled and tugged on the wagon.

Then, Lily's mom came. She saw what was happening and she was not happy. She told Lily and the boy to stop fighting. She told Lily to remove her things from the wagon and give it to the boy. She said Lily had to learn to share and be nice. She said she would buy her a new wagon later.

Lily was sad and mad. She did not want to give up her wagon. She did not want a new wagon. She did not want to share. She cried and stomped her feet. But she had to do what her mom said. She removed her dolls, her books and her snacks from the wagon and gave it to the boy.

The boy was happy. He thanked Lily's mom and said he was sorry. He said he would play with the wagon for a little while and then give it back. He said he would share his ball and his bike with Lily. He said he hoped they could be friends.

Lily did not say anything. She watched the boy play with her wagon. She felt bad and sorry. She wished she had been nicer and shared. She wondered if the boy would really give her wagon back. She wondered if they could really be friends. She learned a lesson that day.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a new girl sitting on a bench. She had a big hat and a book.

"Who is she?" Lily asked Ben.

"I don't know. She looks different," Ben said.

"Let's go and say hello," Lily said. "Maybe she wants to play with us."

Ben was not sure. He thought the new girl might not fit in with them. He followed Lily, but he stayed behind.

"Hi, I'm Lily and this is Ben," Lily said to the new girl. "What's your name?"

"I'm Mia," the new girl said. "I just moved here with my family."

"Where are you from?" Lily asked.

"I'm from Mexico," Mia said. "We speak Spanish at home."

"Wow, that's cool," Lily said. "Can you teach us some Spanish words?"

"Sure, I can," Mia said. She smiled and opened her book. "This is how you say hello: hola."

Lily and Mia started to talk and learn from each other. Ben watched them, but he did not join. He felt left out.

"Ben, come here," Lily called. "Mia is teaching me Spanish. It's fun."

Ben shook his head. He did not want to learn Spanish. He thought it was hard and strange.

"No, thanks," he said. "I like English better."

He walked away and found a well. He looked inside and saw his reflection. He felt lonely and sad.

He wished he had been nicer to Mia. He realized that being different was not bad. He wanted to be friends with her and Lily.

He ran back to the bench and said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I was rude. Can I play with you and Lily?"

Mia and Lily looked at him and smiled.

"Of course, you can," Mia said. "We're happy to include you. You can learn Spanish with us, and we can learn English from you."

"Thank you," Ben said. He sat down and opened his book. "How do you say well in Spanish?"

"Bien," Mia said.

"Bien," Ben repeated. He felt happy and fit.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge people by their appearance or language. Be kind and include everyone. You can learn a lot from different cultures and make new friends.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Lily went first and slid down fast. She laughed and said, "That was fun!" Ben followed her and slid down too. He smiled and said, "Me too!"

Then they saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a big towel on his head and a weird hat on top of it. He was reading a book and did not look at them. Lily and Ben were curious. They walked to the man and pointed at his towel. They asked, "Why do you have a towel on your head?"

The man looked up and saw them. He was not angry. He smiled and said, "Hello, little ones. I have a towel on my head because I have a sore ear. The towel helps it feel better. And I have a hat on top of it because it is cold today. Do you want to see my book?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They liked books. The man showed them his book. It had many pictures and words. He said, "This is a book about animals. Do you like animals?"

Lily and Ben nodded again. They loved animals. They said, "Yes, we do! What is your favorite animal?"

The man said, "My favorite animal is the elephant. It is big and strong and smart. What is yours?"

Lily said, "My favorite animal is the bunny. It is soft and cute and hoppy." Ben said, "My favorite animal is the lion. It is loud and brave and kingy."

The man said, "Those are good choices. All animals are special and wonderful. Do you want to hear a story about them?"

Lily and Ben said, "Yes, please!" They sat next to the man and listened to his story. It was a funny and nice story. They learned a lot and laughed a lot. They forgot about the towel and the hat. They only saw the man and his book.

Their mom came to get them. She said, "It is time to go home, kids. Did you have fun?" Lily and Ben said, "Yes, mom. We met a new friend. He has a towel on his head and a weird hat. But he is very kind and smart. He told us a story about animals. Can we see him again?"

Their mom smiled and said, "Of course, you can. He sounds like a good person. What did you learn from him?"

Lily and Ben said, "We learned that you should not judge people by how they look. You should talk to them and get to know them. You might find out that they have a lot in common with you. And you might make a new friend."

Their mom said, "That is a very good lesson. I am proud of you, kids. Now let's go home and have some snacks. Maybe we can read some more books about animals."

Once upon a time there was an ostrich named Bob. Bob lived in the desert and was content being a desert ostrich. One very hot day, Bob decided to explore the nearby lake. As he cautiously stepped out of the desert sand, he saw an eagle, who had been waiting for him.

The eagle spoke to Bob. "Hello Mr. Ostrich, can I request something of you?" Bob was immediately upset but he answered the eagle's request. "Yes, I'll try," he said.

The eagle said, "I'd like to fly in the air and I can only do that if you give me a ride by standing still and allowing me to perch on your back." Bob was still very upset but he agreed, hoping the eagle would leave him alone soon and he could go back to being a desert ostrich.

Bob immediately started running and the eagle had trouble keeping up. Eventually Bob got so tired he had to stop, and the eagle perched on his back. Bob was very unhappy, and the eagle mocked him. "Thank you Mr. Ostrich, and don't worry, I won't be staying for long."

Bob was relieved and quickly left the eagle as soon as it flew away. Bob decided never again to leave the desert and requested never to have to deal with an eagle again!

"Sure, Timmy. Let's open it together," his mom replied.

As they opened the box, Timmy saw an impressive set of toy cars inside. "Wow, thank you so much, Mommy!" Timmy exclaimed.

"You're welcome, Timmy. I'm glad you like it," his mom said with a smile.

From that day on, Timmy played with his new toy cars every day and always remembered to say thank you to his mom for the wonderful gift.

Once upon a time, there were two bunnies. They both loved to draw with pastel colors, but they drew different things. One bunny drew flowers, and the other bunny drew carrots. 

One day, the bunny who drew flowers saw a pretty pastel buried in the ground. He wanted to keep it for himself, so he didn't tell the other bunny. 

But then, the bunny who drew carrots saw the buried pastel too. He asked the first bunny if he had seen it, but the first bunny lied and said no. 

The second bunny was sad and disappointed. The first bunny realized that lying was not a good thing to do, and he apologized. He dug up the pastel and gave it to the second bunny. From then on, they both shared their pastels and drew together happily. The moral of the story is that it's always better to be honest and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and dirt. One day, she found a caterpillar and decided to take care of it. She put the caterpillar in a jar with some leaves and covered the top with a lid. 

But soon, Lily noticed that the caterpillar wasn't moving much. She realized that it needed oxygen to breathe. So, she took off the lid to let some fresh air in for the caterpillar. 

Days went by and Lily noticed that the jar was getting dirty. She knew that the caterpillar wouldn't like living in a dirty home, so she cleaned the jar with soap and water. The caterpillar was happy and healthy in its clean home and eventually turned into a beautiful butterfly. Lily was so proud of herself for taking care of the caterpillar and giving it a good home.

"Wow, I like your collar," said Fluffy to Spot. "It is very nice."

"Thank you," said Spot, "I like your collar too."

One day, Fluffy and Spot saw a big tree. They wanted to climb the tree. They thought it would be fun. But Fluffy's mom said, "Be careful, little ones. Trees can be dangerous."

Fluffy and Spot did not listen. They climbed the tree, admiring each other's collars as they went up. They were so busy looking at the collars, they did not see the branch that was about to break.

The branch broke, and Fluffy and Spot fell from the tree. They were hurt, and their collars were now dirty and broken. They were very sad. They wished they had listened to Fluffy's mom.

The moral of the story is to always listen to the wise words of others and not to be too focused on things that are not important.

Sam learned his lesson. He started to brush his teeth every day and eat less candy. He also ate fruits and vegetables and drank water. He wanted to keep his teeth healthy and strong. He realized that candy was not worth losing his teeth.

The moral of the story is: You should take care of your teeth and eat a balanced diet. Candy is not good for your teeth. Your teeth are under your gums and they are important for your health and happiness.

Tim and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. One day, they saw a big dragon in the park. The dragon was grumpy. He had a thorn in his tail and it hurt a lot.

"Roar!" the dragon said. "Go away, kids! I don't want to play with you!"

Tim and Mia were scared. They wanted to run away. But they also felt sorry for the dragon. They knew how it felt to have a boo-boo.

"Maybe we can help him," Tim said.

"How?" Mia asked.

"Let's try to pull out the thorn," Tim said.

They walked slowly to the dragon. The dragon saw them and roared again.

"Leave me alone!" he said.

"Please, Mr. Dragon, we want to help you," Mia said. "You have a thorn in your tail and it must hurt a lot. We can pull it out for you."

The dragon looked at them. He saw that they were not mean. They were kind and brave.

"Okay," he said. "But be careful. It might sting."

Tim and Mia took hold of the thorn. They pulled hard. The thorn came out. The dragon felt better.

"Thank you, kids," he said. "You are very nice. I'm sorry I was grumpy. Do you want to play with me?"

Tim and Mia smiled. They nodded. They played with the dragon. They had fun. They learned that sometimes, the best way to make a friend is to help someone in need.

Max shrugged. He did not know the answers. He only knew what he heard from the older kids.

"He lives in a cold place with snow and reindeer," Max said. "He flies in a sleigh at night. He comes down the chimney and puts presents under the tree."

"Can we see Santa?" Lily asked. "Can we talk to him?"

Max shook his head. He said Santa was very busy. He said Santa only came when the kids were asleep.

"Then how can we thank him?" Lily asked.

Max thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"We can write him a letter," Max said. "We can tell him we like the ornament. We can tell him we are good kids. We can ask him for more presents."

Lily liked the idea. She nodded. She and Max ran to get some paper and crayons. They wrote their letter to Santa. They put it on the table near the tree. They hoped Santa would see it. They hoped he would like it. They hoped he would bring them more pretty ornaments.

Tweet flew into the yard and they played all day. They ran and jumped and had lots of fun. When it was time for Tweet to go home, Kitty walked with him to the gate. They said goodbye and Tweet flew away.

Kitty went back to lie in the sun, feeling happy to have a new friend. She knew it was wise to be kind and share her yard with others. And from that day on, Tweet would visit Kitty often, and they would play together by the gate.

One day, a funny dog named Spot went for a run. He liked to run in the park with his big ball. Spot had a round head that made him look very cute. He was always happy when he ran in the park, and he had many friends there.

One day, while Spot was running, he saw a big cat. The cat was not nice. It wanted to take Spot's ball away. Spot did not want to lose his ball, so he thought of a plan.

Spot ran very fast with his ball, and the big cat ran after him. He knew that his friend, a big bird, was near. Spot ran to the big bird, and the bird helped him. The bird flew up high and took the ball away from the cat. The cat could not get the ball, so it went away.

Spot was very happy that his friend helped him. He knew that he could always count on his friends in the park. From that day on, Spot and the big bird played together, and they had lots of fun.

Under the tree, she saw a cute bunny. The bunny was eating a red berry. The girl said, "Hi, bunny! Let's meet and be friends." The bunny looked up and smiled. They played together and had a great time.

After playing, the girl and the bunny were hungry. They found more berries under the tree. They ate the berries and were very happy. They became best friends and played in the park every day.

The tree was very happy. It said "thank you" to Lily. Lily liked the tree too. She came to the tree every day. They became good friends. They played and laughed together. And the tree was never alone again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Bob. Bob loved to sing. Every day, he would sit on a tree branch and sing beautiful songs. One day, while Bob was singing, he saw a big piece of celery on the ground.

Bob flew down to the ground and said, "Hello, celery! Do you want to be my friend?" The celery did not talk, but Bob still wanted to be friends. So, Bob picked up the celery and took it to his nest in the tree.

In the nest, Bob and the celery felt safe. They had a lot of fun together. Bob would sing songs to the celery, and the celery would listen. Even though the celery could not talk or sing, Bob was happy to have a new friend.

One day, a squirrel came to visit Bob and the celery. "Hi, Bob!" said the squirrel. "I see you have a new friend!" Bob smiled and said, "Yes, this is my friend, celery. We like to sing and have fun together."

From that day on, Bob, the celery, and the squirrel all played together in the tree. They felt safe and happy, and Bob loved to sing songs for his friends.

Once upon a time, in a small pond, there lived a little frog named Tim. Tim loved to splash and play all day long. One day, while Tim was splashing in the water, he felt a pain in his stomach. He was worried.

Tim hopped out of the pond to find his friend, Bee. Bee was very smart and always knew what to do. "Bee," said Tim, "my stomach hurts and I am worried." Bee thought for a moment and said, "Maybe you splashed too much. Let's go find some food to make you feel better."

Tim and Bee went to find food for Tim's stomach. They found some yummy bugs for Tim to eat. After eating, Tim felt better and his stomach didn't hurt anymore. Tim said, "Thank you, Bee! You are a good friend." From that day on, Tim learned not to splash too much and to always listen to his friend Bee.

As she swept the dust, it started to go away. Lily felt happy that the dust was gone. She could play outside without the sour feeling on her face. From that day on, Lily always made sure to keep her yard clean and dust-free. And she lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a mop and a broom. They were good friends and always helped to clean the house together. One day, they had a quarrel. The mop said, "I can clean better than you!" The broom replied, "No, I can clean better than you!"

Their quarrel became wild, and they started to fight. They pushed each other around the house, making a big mess. The dust and dirt went everywhere. The house was now dirtier than before.

Just then, a little girl who lived in the house came in. She saw the mess and said, "Oh no! What happened here?" The mop and the broom stopped fighting and looked at the little girl. They felt bad for making the house dirty. They decided to work together and clean up the mess. In the end, the house was clean and shiny again.

The mop and the broom learned that fighting doesn't help anything. They promised to be good friends and work together from that day on. The moral of the story is that working together is better than fighting.
