After a while, Lily's mom said it was time to go home. Lily didn't want to leave the park, so she started to cry. Her mom said, "Don't be spoiled, Lily. We can come back and have more fun tomorrow." Lily stopped crying and said, "Okay, Mommy. I love you." They hugged and went home, singing a happy song together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends in the park. One day, Lily found a yummy olive hidden behind a tree. She ate it all up and felt very happy.

But then, Lily saw a big dog coming towards her. She was scared and didn't know what to do. She tried to step back, but the dog was too fast. It barked loudly and chased after her.

Lily ran as fast as she could, but the dog caught up to her. It bit her leg and she fell down. She cried out for help, but no one came. The dog ran away with the olive in its mouth, leaving poor Lily hurt and alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, she was drawing a beautiful flower when her little brother came into the room. He wanted to play with her crayons, but Lily said no because she was afraid he might break them.

Her brother got angry and started to pull the crayons away from her. Lily tried to lift the crayons up high so he couldn't reach them, but he was too strong. Suddenly, one of the pastel crayons broke in half.

Lily was sad and her brother felt bad too. He said sorry and promised to be careful next time. From that day on, they shared the crayons and drew beautiful pictures together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who lived in a big tree. The bird was very happy and loved to sing all day long. One day, a bad man came and put the bird in a sack. The bird was scared and felt helpless.

The man took the sack with the bird inside and went away. The bird tried to escape, but it was too late. The man took the bird to a place where he sold birds to people who wanted to keep them as pets. The bird was very sad and missed his tree.

Days passed, and the bird never saw his tree again. The people who bought him didn't take good care of him. One day, the bird got very sick and died. The bad man had taken away the bird's happiness and freedom, and now he was gone forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny rocks and pretty flowers. One day, she heard a voice calling her from the woods. It sounded like a bird, but when she got closer, she saw it was a fairy.

The fairy was angry because Lily had picked some of her flowers without asking. The fairy said she would put a curse on Lily and her collection unless she returned the flowers. Lily was scared and ran away, but she didn't return the flowers.

The next day, Lily woke up with a sore throat. She couldn't speak and her voice was gone. She tried to show her collection to her friends, but they couldn't understand her. Lily realized she had made a big mistake by not listening to the fairy. From that day on, she never collected anything without permission again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very bored because he had nothing to do. He sat on the couch and looked at his toes. Timmy wiggled his toes and thought about what he could do.

Suddenly, his mom came in and asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?" Timmy said, "I'm bored." His mom said, "Well, let's guess what we can do to have fun!" Timmy was excited to guess with his mom.

They guessed and guessed until they came up with the best idea. They decided to go outside and play in the park. Timmy was happy again and he wiggled his toes with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a butterfly and wondered where it was going. She followed the butterfly to a garden where she saw a beautiful dress hanging on a tree. 

Lily wanted to try on the dress, but it was too high for her to reach. She decided to climb the tree, but she accidentally tore the dress. It made a big, messy hole in the fabric. 

Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. Just then, the butterfly came back and landed on the dress. It started to flap its wings and magically fixed the hole. Lily was amazed and grateful to the butterfly. From that day on, she made sure to always be careful when climbing trees.

There was a prince who lived in a big castle. He had many toys and books and clothes, but he was not happy. He always wanted more and more. He would demand his servants to bring him new things every day. He would yell and cry if they did not.

One day, a poor girl came to the castle. She had a basket of flowers that she wanted to sell. She knocked on the door and asked if anyone wanted to buy some. The prince heard her and ran to the door. He saw the flowers and liked them. He said, "I want all of them. Give them to me now!"

The girl was scared. She said, "Please, sir, these are my only flowers. I need to sell them to buy food for my family. Can you pay me some coins for them?"

The prince did not care. He said, "No, I will not pay you. You have to give them to me. I am the prince and I can have whatever I want. If you do not, I will call the guards and they will take you away."

The girl was very sad. She did not know what to do. She looked at the prince and said, "Sir, why are you so mean? Don't you have a heart? Don't you know how to share? Don't you know how to be compassionate?"

The prince was surprised. He had never heard that word before. He asked, "What is compassionate?"

The girl said, "Compassionate means to be kind and gentle and caring. To help others who are in need. To be happy with what you have. To be a good person."

The prince thought about it. He realized that he had been selfish and rude. He felt sorry for the girl and her family. He said, "I am sorry. I did not know. I want to be compassionate. Here, you can have your flowers back. And here, take some of my coins too. And some of my toys and books and clothes. You can sell them or keep them. I have enough. Thank you for teaching me a new word and a new way to be."

The girl smiled. She thanked the prince and hugged him. She said, "You are welcome. You are very generous and brave. You can be a good prince and a good friend. I hope to see you again."

The prince smiled too. He felt happy and warm. He said, "I hope so too. Goodbye, my compassionate friend."

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy boats in the pond. They liked to make them sail and race and splash. But then they saw a big duck swimming towards them. The duck looked angry and noisy. It quacked loudly and flapped its wings.

"Go away, duck!" Ben shouted. "These are our boats!"

The duck did not listen. It pecked at Ben's boat and made it sink. Ben cried and ran to his mom. Lily was fearful. She did not want the duck to hurt her boat too.

"Mom, mom, help!" Ben said. "The duck is mean! It broke my boat!"

Mom hugged Ben and dried his tears. She looked at the pond and saw the duck and Lily.

"Lily, come here, sweetie," Mom said. "Let me explain something to you and Ben."

Lily picked up her boat and ran to Mom. She was glad to be safe.

"What is it, Mom?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and said, "The duck is not mean, my loves. It is just hungry and curious. It does not know that your boats are toys. It thinks they are food or friends. It wants to share or play with them."

"Really?" Ben said. "But it hurt my boat!"

"I know, honey, and I'm sorry. But the duck did not mean to. It was just trying to taste or touch your boat. It does not have hands like you. It has a beak and feet. That is how it explores the world."

"Oh," Lily said. "I see. So the duck is not bad?"

"No, sweetie, the duck is not bad. It is just different. And sometimes different can be scary. But if we try to understand and respect the duck, maybe we can be friends with it."

"Friends?" Ben said. "How?"

Mom said, "Well, maybe we can give the duck some bread or seeds. Maybe we can talk to it gently and calmly. Maybe we can watch it swim and learn from it. Maybe we can make a row of boats and let the duck join us."

Lily and Ben liked that idea. They nodded and smiled. They got some bread from Mom and went back to the pond. They threw some pieces to the duck and said, "Hello, duck. We are sorry we yelled at you. We want to be friends with you. Do you want to play with us?"

The duck quacked happily and ate the bread. It swam closer to Lily and Ben and looked at their boats. It did not peck at them anymore. It followed them as they made a row of boats and sailed them together. Lily and Ben laughed and clapped. They were not fearful anymore. They were having fun with the duck.

Ben was miserable. He wanted to go outside and play with his friends, but he could not. Mother had locked the door and said he had to stay inside. She said it was too cold and wet and he would get sick. Ben did not care. He was bored and lonely.

He tried to unlock the door with his toy keys, but they did not work. He tried to push and pull the door, but it did not move. He tried to call his friends, but they did not hear him. He tried to cry, but mother did not come. He sat on the floor and hugged his teddy bear.

Then he heard a knock on the door. He jumped up and ran to the door. He hoped it was his friends, or maybe his father. He looked through the peephole and saw a woman. She had a big smile and a red coat. She waved at him and said, "Hello, Ben. I'm your aunt. Can you open the door for me?"

Ben was confused. He did not know his aunt. He did not know if he should trust her. He looked at her again and saw that she had the same eyes and nose as mother. He remembered that mother had told him about her sister, who lived far away and sometimes visited. He decided to give her a chance.

He reached for the lock and turned it. He heard a click and the door opened. The woman stepped inside and hugged him. She smelled like flowers and cookies. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You're a good boy. I'm sorry I'm late. I came to see you and your mother. Where is she?"

Ben pointed to the bedroom and said, "She's sleeping. She's sick. She locked the door and said I can't go outside."

The woman frowned and said, "Oh, poor mother. And poor you. That's not fair. How about we go and wake her up and see if she feels better? Maybe we can all go outside and have some fun. Would you like that?"

Ben nodded and smiled. He liked his aunt. She was nice and funny. He hoped mother would like her too. He took her hand and led her to the bedroom. He hoped mother would wake up and be happy. He hoped they could all go outside and play. He was not miserable anymore. He was hopeful.

Anna and Ben like to play with water. They have a big hose in the garden. They can spray water from the hose. Sometimes they spray the flowers. Sometimes they spray each other.

One day, they see a big round ball in the sky. It is yellow and bright. It is the sun. Anna and Ben want to spray the sun. They think it will be fun.

They point the hose at the sun. They turn on the water. But the water does not reach the sun. It falls down on them. They get wet and cold.

"Hey, stop it!" Anna says. "You are spraying me!"

"No, you are spraying me!" Ben says. "You are holding the hose!"

They start to fight over the hose. They pull and tug. They forget about the sun.

Mama comes out of the house. She sees Anna and Ben. They are wet and angry. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mama asks. "Why are you spraying water at the sky?"

"We wanted to spray the sun," Anna says.

"We wanted to make it wet," Ben says.

Mama shakes her head. She takes the hose from them. She turns off the water.

"That is not a good idea," Mama says. "The sun is very far away. You cannot spray it. And you should not waste water. Water is important. You need to be more serious."

Anna and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They did not mean to be bad.

"We are sorry, Mama," they say.

Mama smiles. She hugs them. She gives them a towel.

"It's okay," Mama says. "But next time, be more careful. And play nicely. The sun is your friend. It gives you light and warmth. You should not spray it. You should say thank you."

Anna and Ben nod. They dry themselves. They look at the sun. It is still round and bright. They wave at it.

"Thank you, sun," they say.

Their parent opened the door and led them to the living room. There, they saw a big box with a bow on it. It was mysterious and exciting.

Then Lily took the shovel and dug another hole. She put a toy doll in the hole and covered it with dirt. She said, "Tom, can you find the doll?" Tom nodded and started to look for the doll. He used his hands to dig in the dirt. He found the doll and smiled. He said, "I found it, Lily!"

Lily and Max are playing with their toys in the living room. Lily has a doll that can talk and sing. Max has a car that can beep and zoom. They are having fun, but they are also making a lot of noise.

"Be quiet!" Mom says from the kitchen. "I am trying to work on the computer. Your noise is too loud and it hurts my ears."

Lily and Max look at each other. They don't want to make Mom angry, but they also don't want to stop playing. They try to play more quietly, but they still make some noise.

"Be quiet!" Mom says again. "I hate the sound of your toys. It makes me frustrated and I can't think. Go to your room or go outside."

Lily and Max feel sad and confused. They don't understand why Mom hates the sound of their toys. They think their toys are fun and nice. They don't like to go to their room or go outside. They want to stay in the living room and play.

"Mom, we are sorry," Lily says. "We don't mean to make you frustrated. We just want to play with our toys. We love our toys. Why do you hate the sound of our toys?"

Mom sighs and puts down the computer. She walks to the living room and kneels down to hug Lily and Max. She looks at their toys and smiles.

"I don't really hate the sound of your toys," she says. "I just don't like it when it is too loud and it distracts me from my work. I know your toys are fun and nice, and I love you very much. But sometimes I need some quiet time to do my work. Can you understand that?"

Lily and Max nod. They understand that Mom needs some quiet time, just like they need some play time. They hug Mom back and say they are sorry.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big poster. It said: "Come and see the lion show! Only five coins!"

"Wow, a lion show!" Tom said. "I want to see the lions. They are big and strong and loud."

"Me too," Sam said. "But we don't have five coins. We only have two."

"Maybe we can find more coins," Tom said. "Let's look around the park."

They looked under the benches, in the trash cans, and on the ground. They found three more coins. They were very happy.

"Yay, we have enough coins!" Sam said. "Let's go to the lion show."

They ran to the poster. There was a man with a hat and a coat. He took their coins and gave them two tickets.

"Here you go, kids," he said. "The lion show is in that tent. Enjoy!"

Tom and Sam went inside the tent. It was dark and smelly. They saw a cage with a lion inside. The lion was very thin and sad. He had no fur on his tail and his eyes were dull.

"Is this the lion show?" Tom asked.

"Yes, it is," the man said. "You can watch the lion for ten minutes. Then you have to leave."

"That's not a show," Sam said. "That's a cheap trick. You are mean to the lion. You don't support him. You don't give him food or water or love."

"Shut up, kid," the man said. "You don't know anything. The lion is fine. He likes his cage. Now be quiet or I'll make you leave."

Tom and Sam felt sorry for the lion. They wanted to help him. They looked for a way to open the cage. They saw a lock and a key on the wall.

"Maybe we can free the lion," Tom whispered. "Maybe he can run away and find a better home."

"OK, let's try," Sam whispered. "But be careful. The lion might be angry or scared."

They waited for the man to look away. Then they ran to the wall and grabbed the key. They put it in the lock and turned it. The cage door opened.

"Roar!" the lion roared. He jumped out of the cage and ran to the tent flap. He tore it with his claws and escaped.

"Hey, what are you doing?" the man shouted. He ran after the lion. He tried to catch him.

But the lion was faster and stronger. He turned around and bit the man's arm. He made him bleed and cry.

"Help! Help!" the man screamed. "The lion is attacking me!"

Tom and Sam were scared. They wanted to run away. But they were too late. The lion saw them and ran to them. He was hungry and angry. He did not like them. He did not thank them. He did not care.

He opened his mouth and ate them.

They could build anything they wanted with the blocks, like houses, cars, or animals. Their mom and dad gave them the blocks as a gift, and told them to take good care of them.

But before they could call them, they heard a loud knock on the door. It was their cousin Sam, who came to visit them.

Sam was older than Tim and Jen, and he did not like to play with blocks. He thought they were boring and babyish. He wanted to play with something else, like a video game or a bike. He saw the tower of blocks, and he had a mean idea. He pushed the tower with his hand, and made it fall down. The blocks scattered all over the floor, making a big mess.

Tim and Jen were very sad and angry. They cried and shouted at Sam. "Why did you do that? You broke our tower! You are a bad cousin!" Sam did not care. He laughed and said, "It's just a bunch of blocks. They are not worth anything. You can buy more with a little price. Stop being so serious."

Mom and dad heard the noise, and came to the room. They saw the scattered blocks, and the crying twins, and the laughing Sam. They were very disappointed and upset. They scolded Sam, and told him to apologize to Tim and Jen. They also told him to help them clean up the mess. Sam did not want to, but he had no choice. He said sorry to Tim and Jen, but he did not mean it. He helped them pick up the blocks, but he did not do a good job. He left some blocks under the bed, and some behind the door.

The next day, Sam wanted to play with his bike. He asked mom and dad if he could borrow their bike pump, because his tire was flat. They said yes, and told him where to find it. It was in the closet, next to the door. Sam opened the closet, and reached for the pump. But he did not see the blocks that he left behind the door. He stepped on them, and slipped. He fell down, and hit his head on the closet. He felt a lot of pain, and started to cry.

Mom and dad heard the cry, and came to the closet. They saw Sam on the floor, with a bump on his head, and the blocks around him. They realized what happened, and shook their heads. They helped Sam get up, and put some ice on his bump. They also told him a lesson. "You see, Sam, what you did was wrong. You should not have ruined Tim and Jen's tower. You should not have lied about the price of the blocks. You should not have laughed at their feelings. You should have been more careful and respectful. And now, you have to pay the price of your actions. You have to suffer the pain of your fall. You have to learn to be more serious."

Sam felt sorry for what he did, and wished he could take it back. But it was too late. He had to live with the consequences of his choices. He learned a hard lesson that day, and he hoped he would never forget it. He also hoped that Tim and Jen would forgive him, and that they would still play with him. He decided to be a better cousin, and a better person, from then on.

Their mom and dad came out. They hugged them and said "It's okay, it's okay. You did a great job. You sold a lot of cocoa. You made a lot of people happy. You can try again another day. Come on, let's go inside and have some cocoa. We have some more in the kitchen."

So, the lion and the frog hopped together all day long. They hopped over rocks, they hopped over logs, and they hopped through the tall grass. They had so much fun hopping that they became best friends. And from that day on, the lion and the frog always hopped together in the tidy forest.

Tim learned that if he stored his toys away, he could find the important old car easily. He also saw that his room was clean and nice. Tim felt happy and proud. The moral of the story is to take care of your things and store them away, so you can find what is important when you need it.

A sleepy owl heard Bobo and said, "Yawn! That hole is for the big race tomorrow. The first one to the end is the success."

Bobo wanted to be the success. The next day, all the animals came to race. They ran and ran, but Bobo was very fast. He hopped and hopped until he reached the end. All the animals cheered for Bobo.

Bobo was so happy that he was the success. He said, "Thank you, friends, for cheering for me!" And from that day on, Bobo was known as the fastest bunny in the forest.

One day, Lily found a shiny gem near the river. It was so pretty that she wanted to show it to her friend, Tom. She ran to Tom's house and said, "Look, I found a gem! It's so pretty!" Tom looked at the gem and said, "Wow, it's so shiny! Let's go find more!"

So, Lily and Tom went to the river to find more gems. They found many small gems, but then they saw a big, beautiful gem in the water. They tried to get it, but it was too far away. Lily wished she could become a fish to swim and get the gem.

Suddenly, a magical fish appeared and said, "I can help you, Lily. If you promise to be obedient and always listen to your mom and dad, I will make you a fish for a short time." Lily agreed, and she became a fish. She swam in the river and got the big gem.

Lily and Tom were so happy with their gems. They thanked the magical fish and went home to show their parents. Lily learned that being obedient can sometimes lead to magical adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She was a deaf daughter of a kind man and woman. Lily loved to skip and play with her friends.

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe it is a new friend. Let's go say hello."

But the big, gray thing was not a friend. It was a shark. And the shark was hungry and ignorant. It did not care about Tim and Tom. It only wanted to eat them.

The shark saw the two fish and opened its mouth. It swam fast and tried to catch them. Tim and Tom were scared and tried to swim away. They looked for a place to hide.

"Help!" Tim cried.

"Help!" Tom cried.

They saw a big rock with a hole in it. They swam inside the hole and hoped the shark would not find them. The shark was angry and tried to bite the rock. But the rock was hard and the shark hurt its teeth. It swam away and looked for other food.

Tim and Tom were safe and happy. They hugged each other and thanked the rock.

"Thank you, rock," Tim said.

"Thank you, rock," Tom said.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that not all things in the sea are friendly. And they learned that sharks are ignorant and mean. They decided to stay away from sharks and to stick with their friends.

Tom and Sara smile. They are good kids. They are safe and loved. They are happy.

Sara and Ben nodded and said, "We love you too, Mom. And we learned our lesson. Cherries are good, but safety is better."

Once upon a time there were two vines - one was tall and strong, and the other was small and weak.

The tall vine said, "If you accept me as your teacher, I will teach you how to spread your roots and reach the light."
The small vine agreed and the tall vine began teaching it how to grow.

The small vine listened diligently and followed the tall vine's instructions. Soon, it had spread its roots deep into the earth, soaking up nourishment, and it was able to reach the light and soak up its energy.

Before long, the small vine was as tall and strong as its teacher, and the two were now friends, admiring each other's growth.

This story teaches us that with patience and motivation, anything is possible, and the things that seem impossible at first can be accomplished with hard work, a positive attitude, and help from friends. So, if you have a dream, never give up! Accept the help of others and have faith in your own abilities. With time and effort, you can reach the light.

It was a lively day and Bob was looking forward to the exciting things that would happen. He was happy that his grandma had arrived to spend the day with him. He and his grandma spent the day running and playing in the park. When it was time to leave, Bob noticed a bottle of juice under a bench. 

Bob asked his grandma if he could take the bottle of juice home with him. His grandma said yes and Bob was excited. 

When Bob and his grandma got home, Bob took the bottle into the kitchen and put it in the refrigerator. Then Bob asked his grandma for something special. He wanted her to help him open the bottle. 

Bob was so surprised when he opened the bottle and found a hidden surprise inside! There was a toy fire truck that was so lively and exciting. He had never seen a toy like it before. His grandma explained that she had put the fire truck in the bottle before they went to the park. She had known the whole time that the bottle would have an exciting surprise inside.

Once there was a man with a mustache. He was very careful and always thought before he acted. One day he was walking in the park and saw a bird blinking at him. The man smiled and said hello to the bird. The bird blinked again and flew away. The man was sad and missed the bird. He wanted to make the bird happy, so he grabbed some food from his pocket and waited for the bird to return. The bird flew back and blinked again and ate the food. The man and the bird became friends and the bird blinked at the man whenever it saw him. The man was happy because he made the bird happy. They were the best of friends.

But just then, something happened. A noise filled the sky and the man stopped to look. It was the treasure's guardian -- a giant dragon! The dragon was very angry, roaring and breathing fire. The man was so scared he dropped the treasure and ran away. 

The dragon then picked up the treasure and flew away. The man was sad and never got his treasure. He learnt that greed can lead to a very bad end.

One day, Tom was walking down the road. He was feeling grumpy and had nothing better to do. Suddenly, he stopped, and got down on his knees in front of a little pond. He saw a frog lurking in the water and decided to talk to it.

"Hi there! What's your name?" asked Tom.

The frog hopped closer and said "Kermit!"

Tom was very happy, and he said "It's nice to meet you, Kermit. Can I kneel here and talk with you?"

Kermit nodded, so Tom knelt down beside the pond. They talked for the rest of the afternoon. Tom forgot about how grumpy he was before, and by the time he left, he felt much happier.

Once, there was a 3-year-old girl named Lucy. She loved her toys and spent most of her days playing with them. One day, she wanted to play with her toy boat, but it was made out of steel, so she couldn't push it around the house. 

She thought for a moment and then had an idea. Lucy scurried to the kitchen and grabbed a wooden spoon. She ran back with the spoon and tried to use it to push the boat around, but it was too heavy. 

Lucy started to grow impatient. She scrunched up her face and frowned. It looked like this wasn't going to work. 

Just then, her father walked into the room. "Hey, Lucy," he said. "Do you need any help?" Lucy looked up and nodded. She handed him the spoon and he showed her how to be gentle as she tried to push the boat. 

With some help from her father, Lucy was soon playing happily with her boat. She was no longer frowning.

Mom said, "No, it's too dangerous for you to go by yourself."

Jim didn't want to listen. He asked again, and this time his mom said yes.

Once he got out of the village, Jim spotted a big fox. He was scared but brave at the same time. He decided to kick the fox away. He kicked the fox so hard that it ran back into the woods. Jim felt very proud of himself.

He continued to explore the village, but at every turn he found something more dangerous than the fox. He saw a wild boar that looked ready to charge. Jim felt scared, but he remembered what he learned - he had to stay brave. He kicked the boar as hard as he could and it ran away.

From then on, Jim was the bravest boy in the village. He never backed down from danger, and he always stayed bold and brave.

One day, Tom and his mother were in the yard. It was getting very dark outside, and Tom started to feel a little scared. He asked his mother, "Mommy, why are the birds still up?"

His mother smiled and said, "Those birds know what to do in the dark, Tom. They are getting ready to go to sleep and tomorrow, when the sun comes up, they will sing again."

Tom thought about this for a moment and then he said, "Mommy, can we pray?"

"Of course we can," his mother said.

So she and Tom sat in the yard and held hands. Even though Tom was still a little fearful, he felt more peaceful as they prayed. Then they said "Amen" and his mother kissed him goodnight.

The next day, when Tom woke up, he could hear the birds singing from the yard. He smiled and knew that his prayer had worked.

But then Jack noticed something bad. The soil was getting all mixed up with the stones and leaves. Soon there was no soil left to play with. 

Jack was sad, so she asked her mum if she could please have more soil to play with. Her mum smiled and said yes. She went and bought Jack a big bag of soil so she could keep on playing and building sandcastles.

Jack was so happy and thanked her mum for getting her the soil. She made even bigger sandcastles that day and never let the bad soil stop her from playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny. The bunny was very careful and always hopped in neat little hops. One day, while hopping along, the bunny came across a big, green leaf. Curious, the bunny nudged the leaf and it started to move. Suddenly, a big, furry creature popped out from under the leaf! The bunny was so scared it hopped away very quickly.

The little creature was a squirrel. It stood up tall and looked around. Although it was quite startled at first, the squirrel soon saw the bunny and felt safe. It happily started to nibble on the leaves around it.

The bunny watched on, not wanting to disturb the squirrel any more. The bunny hopped away, carefully avoiding the leaf, and continued hopping until it reached its home. From then on, the bunny was extra careful with every leaf it came across.

Once upon a time there was a teddy bear who wanted to knit a scarf for his friend, a bunny. But where would he find the yarn? He searched high, but there was no yarn to be found. He searched low, but still nothing. He shrugged in despair. 

Suddenly, he had an idea. He walked over to the nearby bridge and said, "Excuse me, bridge - do you have any yarn I can use?"

The bridge thought for a moment and then replied, "I am afraid that I am made of metal and do not have any yarn. But if you look under the bridge, you can maybe find some sticks and reeds that are flexible. You can use them to make a scarf for your friend!"

And so, the teddy bear did just that. He used the flexible sticks and reeds to weave a clever scarf for the bunny. The bunny was so pleased with the gift! 

The moral of this story is that sometimes we need to look in unexpected places and be flexible to find solutions to our problems.

The dust from the closet had made Sammy very sick. He tried to get away, but he was stuck in the wide closet. It seemed like nothing could help him.

In the end, Sammy got very sick from the dust in the closet and his parents had to take him to the hospital. Sadly, Sammy never returned home from the hospital. Foreshadowing the bad ending, the old dusty closet had been the source of his misfortune.

One day, a little girl came up to him. She seemed kind and he could see that she wanted to care for him. He cautiously waited as she picked him up and held him close. The girl brought the dish with her everywhere she went.

The dish and the girl spent each day together. Whenever she was feeling sad, she would bring the dish out and stroke it with her finger. He was happy to have someone who wanted to care for him.

But then one day, the little girl had to leave. She ran off to somewhere distant, like the dish's life had been before her. He was sad now, and he didn't know what to do.

But then the girl appeared one day with a smile on her face. She brought a gift with her and her mother, too. It was a special caring dish. The girl and her mother put it in the same spot as the lonely dish, so that each one could be cared for. The distant life of the dish was no more.

"What are we looking for?" asked John.

"Something exciting!" replied Dad.

They stepped over a log and saw a big owl. It was perched high up in a tree. John was amazed.

"Wow, Dad. Look at that big owl!" said John.

Dad smiled. He looked up and smiled even wider.

"That means something exciting is going to happen!" said Dad.

John was confused, but he followed Dad further down the path. Then he heard a rustling in the trees and started to get excited. Suddenly, a whole family of big owls flew out of the trees! John was amazed. 

"What did you do, Dad?" asked John, excitedly.

"I just made a guess," said Dad. "I thought that if we found one big owl, there must be more around."

John laughed with delight. He was very glad he had come walking with Dad that day. He was sure he would find something exciting.

From then on out, Joe was never scared to look closer and find out what wonderful things were waiting for him. The moral of the story is that often what we think is scary can turn out to be amazing if we take the time to look closer.

From that day on, the princess never wore a veil again. She learned that true beauty comes from being kind and humble, not from what you wear on your face. The princess and the farmer became good friends and they lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter. He was very stupid. He went into the forest to hunt a big bear. But he didn't know where to look. He walked and walked until he got tired. Then he sat down under a tree and fell asleep.

While the hunter was sleeping, a little bird came and sat on his head. The bird saw the hunter's gun and wanted to play with it. So the bird pecked at the gun until it came apart. The hunter didn't wake up.

When the hunter woke up, he saw that his gun was in pieces. He was very angry. He looked around and saw the little bird. He ran after the bird, but the bird flew away. The hunter never found his gun parts and he never caught the big bear.

Kitty told Bunny not to worry. She said, "We all have different things we are good at. You are very fast and smart!" Bunny felt better and learned that it is okay to be different. They played happily together, and Bunny did not worry anymore.

But, Max started to feel jealous. He wanted Mia all to himself. So, Max took the ball and hid it. Mia and Sam looked for the ball but couldn't find it. Max came out with the ball and said, "Woof! Woof!" Mia understood that Max wanted to play with her alone. She told Sam, "Max wants to play with me now. Let's play together another time." Sam said, "Okay, see you later, Mia!" And Mia and Max played happily together again.

Tom said to his friend, the dog, "Give me that old toy! I want to play with it!" The dog looked sad but did what Tom said. Tom started to play with the old toy, but he did not share it with the dog.

Soon, the other animals did not want to play with Tom. They did not like how bossy he was. Tom felt sad and lonely. He thought about what he did and decided to change. He gave the old toy back to the dog and said, "I am sorry for being bossy. Let's play together."

The dog was happy, and they played together. The other animals saw Tom was not bossy anymore, and they all played together too. The moral of the story is that sharing and being kind to others is important.

So, they made a jug out of clay and let it dry. Lily painted a beautiful picture of the jug. Later, they put some cold water in the jug and drank it together. Lily learned that when you want to do something, you can find a way to make it happen.

Once upon a time, there was a little turtle named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the pond with his friends. One day, Timmy found a big shell that was too thick for him to open. He asked his friends for help, but they couldn't open it either.

Lily learned that it's important to listen to her dad and not to approach wild animals. She realized that it's better to raise awareness about protecting animals and the environment than to try and play with them.

Ben puts the chess set in a box. He closes the box with a tight lid. He puts the box under his bed. He thinks, "I am lucky to have a friend like Lily. She trusts me with her chess set. I will not let her down. I will return it to her tomorrow."

The next day, Lily comes back to Ben's house. She knocks on the door. Ben opens the door. He smiles and says, "Hello, Lily. I am glad you are here. Do you want to play chess?"

Lily says, "Yes, I do. Where is my chess set?"

Ben says, "It is under my bed. I will get it for you." He goes to his room. He pulls out the box. He opens the box. He gasps. He sees that the chess set is gone. There are only some crumbs and a hole in the box. He thinks, "Oh no! A mouse ate the chess set. How did this happen? What will I tell Lily?"

He runs back to the door. He sees Lily waiting. He feels sad and sorry. He says, "Lily, I have bad news. Your chess set is gone. A mouse ate it. I am so sorry. I did not mean to lose it. I did not mean to break it. I wanted to return it to you. Please forgive me."

Lily looks at Ben. She sees that he is telling the truth. She sees that he is sorry. She feels sad too. She says, "Ben, I am sad that my chess set is gone. I liked it very much. But I am not angry with you. I know you did not do it on purpose. I know you tried to take good care of it. I know you wanted to return it to me. You are still my friend. I forgive you."

Ben hugs Lily. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. You are still my friend too. I am sorry for your loss. I will try to make it up to you. Maybe we can find another chess set. Maybe we can play another game. Maybe we can have fun again."

Lily smiles. She says, "Yes, Ben. We can do that. We can still have fun. We can still play. We can still be friends."

The moral of the story is: Friendship is more important than things. Things can be lost or broken, but friends can be forgiven and trusted. Friends should be honest and kind to each other. Friends should share and return what they borrow. Friends should have fun and learn together.

Tim and Sue wanted to make a pumpkin pie for their mom. They went to the farm to buy a pumpkin. They saw many pumpkins, but they wanted the largest one. They found a large pumpkin that was bigger than their heads.

"Can we have this pumpkin, please?" Tim asked the farmer.

The farmer smiled and said, "Sure, you can have it. But it is very heavy. You will need a cart to carry it."

Tim and Sue did not have a cart. They tried to lift the pumpkin, but it was too hard. They could not move it.

"Maybe we should choose a smaller pumpkin," Sue said.

But Tim did not want to give up. He said, "No, we want this one. It is the best pumpkin for our pie. We can drag it to our home."

Tim and Sue started to drag the pumpkin on the ground. It was very slow and tiring. They scraped the pumpkin and made it dirty. They also made a mess on the road. They did not notice the other people and animals who were trying to pass by. They bumped into them and made them angry.

"Hey, watch out!" a man shouted.

"Ouch, you hurt me!" a dog barked.

"Sorry, sorry," Tim and Sue said. But they did not stop dragging the pumpkin.

They finally reached their home. They were very happy. They knocked on the door and said, "Mom, look what we have! A large pumpkin for our pie!"

Mom opened the door and saw the pumpkin. She was not happy. She said, "What have you done? This pumpkin is too big for our oven. And it is all scratched and dirty. And why did you drag it on the ground? You have been rude and selfish. You did not think of the farmer who supplied you the pumpkin, or the other people and animals who shared the road with you. You only thought of yourselves. That is not how you make a pumpkin pie. That is how you make a pumpkin mess."

Tim and Sue felt ashamed. They realized they had made a mistake. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We wanted to make you happy, but we did not think of others. We were greedy and foolish. Can we fix it?"

Mom sighed and said, "Well, you can start by apologizing to the farmer and the others you have annoyed. Then you can clean the pumpkin and cut it into smaller pieces. Maybe we can still make a small pie with some of it. But you have to learn to be grateful and respectful. A large pumpkin is not always better than a small one. It is what you do with it that matters."

Tim and Sue nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We have learned our lesson. Thank you for teaching us. We love you."

Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too. Now let's go and make things right."

Just then, a big cat named Fluffy came along. "What's wrong, little mouse?" Fluffy asked. "I'm stuck in this trap and it's leaking," Timmy said. "Can you help me?" Fluffy smiled and said, "Of course I can help you, little mouse." But instead of helping, Fluffy pinched Timmy's tail and ate the cheese. Timmy was very sad and learned to be careful around cats.

One day, a rabbit named Benny was very hungry. He hopped around looking for something delicious to eat. Suddenly, he saw a big carrot in a garden. Benny quickly ran to the garden and started eating the carrot. 

Just then, a farmer saw Benny eating his carrot. The farmer was very angry and shouted, "Bad rabbit! You ate my carrot! I will punish you!" Benny felt scared and ran away as fast as he could.

Benny met his friend, a little bird, on the way. Benny told the bird what had happened and how he was punished for eating the carrot. The bird said, "Don't worry, Benny! You can come to my treehouse and we can share some of my delicious seeds." Benny felt happy and followed the bird to his treehouse. They had a fun time eating together and Benny forgot all about the punishment.

So they all chased after Browny. He flew around the forest and they ran after him, trying to catch him. But after a while, they gave up.

Browny was very happy that nobody had caught him. He flew away to his meadow and enjoyed the rest of the day with his friends.

After playing in the puddle, the king went back to his castle. He remembered to take off his wet crown and put it in the sun to dry. The king was happy because he had so much fun in the puddle. And he knew that his shiny crown would be dry soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little spider. The spider had many friends in the garden. But the spider was sometimes selfish. It did not like to share its things with its friends.

One day, the spider found a big, colorful ball. It was very happy and wanted to play with it all day. The spider did not allow its friends to play with the ball. The friends were sad and did not play with the spider anymore.

The spider soon felt lonely and realized it was wrong to be selfish. It decided to share the ball with its friends. The friends were very happy, and they all played together. The spider learned that sharing was more fun than being selfish.

Lily was a careless girl. She liked to run and play without looking where she was going. While playing, she bumped into a kind farmer. The farmer was holding a big bowl, and he was mixing something.

"Oops! I'm sorry!" said Lily. The farmer smiled and said, "That's okay, little one. I'm just mixing food for the animals. Would you like to help me?"

Lily nodded and helped the farmer mix the corn with other food. They fed the animals together, and Lily learned to be more careful. From that day on, Lily always remembered to watch where she was going and to help others when she could.

While they were painting, a little boy came up to them. "Wow, that's a beautiful painting!" he said. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you! We're painting the tree because I wondered how tall it was." The little boy thought that was cool and asked if he could help. Lily and her mom said yes, and they all painted together. They had so much fun painting and wondering about the world around them.

She remembered that she had a big ball in her bag. She took out the ball and started to play catch with her friends. They had so much fun!

Even though they didn't have the swings and slides, they still had a great time in the park. They ran around and played games. Ellie was happy that she could help her friends have fun. They all went home with big smiles on their faces, looking forward to the next time they could play together in the park.

The bear thought and thought, trying to guess where he might have left his hammer. Suddenly, he remembered that he had left it by the river when he was fishing. He was happy that he had guessed correctly! He went to the river and found his hammer. From then on, he was more careful and did not lose his things anymore.

The reindeer stopped and looked down at him. It seemed to acknowledge him and then it began to run again. It flew across the sky and soon became a tiny little speck.

Jack followed the bird's advice and went home. He met with his family and talked about what he had learned. They listened to him and finally figured out how to be happy.

From then on, Jack never suffered again and his family were happy. The bird had helped him find the courage to make things better. Jack was so glad that he felt no shame.

Bob said, "But we can use it to cut branches and make a shelter when we camp."

Jack replied, "No, I don't think so, we don't need to carry it."

Bob insisted, "But it's an ancient axe, and it could be really useful!"

Jack shook his head, he still disagreed. He said, "I'm sure there are other ways we can make a shelter, so let's just leave the axe here in the forest."

Finally, Bob reluctantly agreed and they continued on their journey, leaving the axe in the ancient forest.

Suddenly, Lily had an idea. She asked her dad for the rake and began to scatter the leaves around their picnic blanket. It was just like playing in her backyard! Lily's dad smiled and said, "You're so clever, Lily. I'm glad we brought the rake with us."

Lily was happy that she could still play in the leaves, even at the park. And she learned that sometimes the things we think we don't need can come in handy later on.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to make some eggs for breakfast. They went to the kitchen and found some eggs in the fridge.

"Can you help me, Ben?" Lily asked. "We need to crack the eggs and put them in a pan."

"OK, Lily," Ben said. "I can crack the eggs. You can hold the pan."

They worked together to crack the eggs and put them in the pan. Then they looked for the stove.

"Where is the stove, Lily?" Ben asked. "We need to cook the eggs on the stove."

Lily pointed to a big thing with four circles on top. "That is the stove, Ben," she said. "We need to turn on one of the circles. Then it will get hot and cook the eggs."

They walked to the stove and looked at the circles. One of them was bright. It was red and shiny.

"Look, Ben," Lily said. "That circle is bright. It is on. We can put the pan on it."

But before they could do that, they heard a loud voice.

"Stop, Lily and Ben!" It was Mom. She ran to the kitchen and saw what they were doing. She was scared and angry.

"What are you doing, Lily and Ben?" Mom asked. "You can't use the stove by yourselves. It is very dangerous. You could get burned or start a fire. You need to ask me first if you want to cook something."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not know the stove was dangerous. They just wanted to make some eggs.

"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We were hungry. We wanted to make some eggs for breakfast."

Mom hugged them and said, "I know, Lily and Ben. But you need to be careful in the kitchen. The stove is not a toy. It is only for grown-ups. Next time, you need to wait for me or Dad. We can make some eggs together. OK?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "OK, Mom. We will wait for you or Dad. We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. Now, let's make some eggs together. And some toast. And some juice. How does that sound?"

Lily and Ben clapped their hands and said, "That sounds yummy, Mom. Thank you, Mom."

They helped Mom to make some eggs for breakfast. They ate them with toast and juice. They were happy and full. They learned a lesson about the stove. They never used it by themselves again.

The dog waited for the right moment. He moved the spot to the door. He made a loud noise. He opened the door. He ran inside. He barked at Tom. He chased him.

Tom was very surprised. He was very afraid. He ran away. He hid under the bed. He wished he had never seen the spot. He wished he had fur on his head. He wished he had a friend. He wished he had no dogs.

Sara and Ben were playing with blocks. They liked to make towers and bridges and houses. Sara had a lot of red blocks and Ben had a lot of blue blocks. They decided to play a game.

"I will make a shape with my blocks and you will guess what it is," Sara said. "Then you will make a shape and I will guess."

"OK, that sounds fun," Ben said. "You go first."

Sara took four red blocks and put them together. She made a shape with four sides and four corners. She showed it to Ben.

"What is this shape?" Sara asked.

Ben looked at the shape. He thought for a moment. He remembered what his teacher had told him.

"That is a square," Ben said. "I know because it has four sides and four corners that are the same."

"Very good, Ben," Sara said. "You are right. It is a square. Now you make a shape and I will guess."

Ben took four blue blocks and put them together. He made a shape with four sides and four corners, but the sides and corners were not the same. He showed it to Sara.

"What is this shape?" Ben asked.

Sara looked at the shape. She was confused. She did not know what it was. She tried to guess.

"Is it a...circle?" Sara said.

Ben laughed. "No, it is not a circle. A circle has no sides and no corners. It is round."

Sara felt ashamed. She did not like to be wrong. She did not like to be laughed at.

"Is it a...triangle?" Sara said.

Ben laughed again. "No, it is not a triangle. A triangle has three sides and three corners. It is pointy."

Sara felt more ashamed. She did not want to play anymore. She wanted to cry.

"Is it a...square?" Sara said.

Ben stopped laughing. He looked at Sara. He saw that she was sad. He felt sorry for her.

"No, it is not a square. A square has four sides and four corners that are the same. It is flat."

"Then what is it?" Sara said.

Ben smiled. He wanted to make Sara happy. He wanted to be a good friend.

"It is a diamond," Ben said. "It is a special shape. It is like a square, but it is tilted. It is shiny and pretty. Do you like it?"

Sara looked at the shape. She saw that it was different from a square. She saw that it was shiny and pretty. She smiled.

"Yes, I like it," Sara said. "It is a nice shape. Thank you for telling me. I did not know it was a diamond."

Ben hugged Sara. He was glad that she was happy. He was glad that they were friends.

"You are welcome," Ben said. "I am sorry for laughing at you. You are very smart. You knew what a square was. I did not know what a diamond was until my teacher told me. Do you want to play some more?"

Sara nodded. She was not ashamed anymore. She was curious.

"Yes, I want to play some more," Sara said. "Can you show me some other shapes?"

Ben nodded. He was happy. He liked to share.

Lena was a modest sheep who lived on a farm with many other sheep. She liked to eat grass, play with her friends and listen to the farmer's stories. She did not care much about how she looked or what others thought of her.

One day, the farmer came to shear the sheep and take their wool. He praised Lena for having the softest and finest wool of all. He said he would make a special sweater for his granddaughter with her wool. Lena felt happy and proud, but she did not boast or show off.

However, some of the other sheep were jealous of Lena. They thought she was too plain and boring. They started to tease her and call her names. They said she was a weakling, a dullard and a brown-noser. They made fun of her wool and her modesty.

Lena felt hurt and sad. She did not understand why they were so mean to her. She tried to ignore them, but they did not stop. She wished they would leave her alone.

One day, she decided to talk to the farmer. She asked him why he liked her wool so much. He smiled and said, "Lena, your wool is not only soft and fine, but also warm and strong. It is perfect for making a cozy sweater for my granddaughter, who lives in a cold place. She will love it and cherish it. You see, your wool is not just wool, it is a gift of love."

Lena felt touched and grateful. She realized that the farmer was right. Her wool was not just wool, it was a gift of love. She also realized that the other sheep were wrong. They did not know the true value of her wool or her modesty. They only cared about how they looked or what others thought of them.

She decided to forgive them and be kind to them. She hoped they would learn to appreciate their own wool and their own gifts. She also hoped they would learn to be more modest and respectful of others.

The moral of the story is: Modesty is a virtue that makes us humble and grateful. It also makes us more valuable and lovable. We should not judge others by their appearance or their possessions, but by their character and their actions. We should also not let others' jealousy or mockery affect our self-esteem or happiness. We should be proud of who we are and what we have, and share our gifts with love.

One day, Lily and her grandma heard a loud noise outside. They ran to the window and saw a big truck with men who wanted to take Daisy away. The men said they needed the cow for their farm and they would pay some money for her.

Lily and her grandma were very sad and scared. They did not want to lose Daisy, but they also needed money to buy food and clothes. Lily hugged Daisy and said, "Please don't go, Daisy. You are my friend and I love you."

Daisy heard Lily and felt her love. She did not want to go either. She used her horns to push the men away and then she sprang over the fence. She ran to the woods where she knew there was a safe place to hide.

Lily and her grandma followed Daisy and found her in a clearing with some other cows. The cows were friendly and shared their grass and water with Daisy. Lily and her grandma smiled and thanked them. They decided to stay with Daisy and the other cows and live in the woods. They did not need money or a big house. They had milk, food, friends and love. They were happy.

Emma smiled and said, "OK, I will be gentle. What are you doing with Lily?"

Emma said, "Yes, I want to learn. How do you teach Lily how to dance?"

Lila was a princess who liked to wear a veil. She thought it made her look pretty and special. She liked to play with her veil and pretend she was in a fairy tale.

One day, she invited her friend Tom to her castle. Tom was a knight who liked to fight dragons and save princesses. He brought his sword and shield and was ready for an adventure.

"Hello, Princess Lila," he said. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, Knight Tom," she said. "But first, you have to see my veil. It is very nice and shiny."

She showed him her veil and put it on her head. She smiled and twirled around.

Tom looked at her veil and frowned. He did not think it was nice or shiny. He thought it was silly and boring.

"Why do you wear that?" he asked. "It covers your face and hair. You can't see anything or do anything with it. It is not fun at all."

Lila felt hurt and angry. She liked her veil and she wanted Tom to like it too. She did not want him to make fun of her.

"That's not true," she said. "My veil is fun and pretty. It makes me happy. You are mean and rude. You don't understand anything."

She took off her veil and threw it at him. Then she ran away and hid behind a curtain.

Tom was surprised and sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lila or make her cry. He liked her and he wanted to play with her. He did not understand why she liked her veil so much.

He picked up her veil and looked at it. He saw that it was soft and sparkly. He saw that it had flowers and stars on it. He saw that it was Lila's favorite thing.

He felt ashamed and sad. He wanted to say sorry and make her happy again.

He walked to the curtain and peeked behind it. He saw Lila sitting on the floor, wiping her eyes.

"Princess Lila," he said softly. "I'm sorry. I was wrong. Your veil is very nice and shiny. It is not silly or boring. It is fun and pretty. It makes you happy. And I want you to be happy. Can you forgive me? Can we still be friends? Can we still play together?"

Lila looked at him and saw that he was holding her veil. She saw that he was sincere and kind. She saw that he was her friend.

She smiled and nodded. She took her veil and put it on her head. She got up and hugged him.

"Thank you, Knight Tom," she said. "I forgive you. You are not mean or rude. You are nice and sweet. You understand me. We are still friends. We can still play together."

They hugged and laughed. They played and had fun. They shared their veil and their sword and their shield. They pretended they were in a fairy tale. And they were happy.

The other clowns nodded and smiled. But one of them was very naughty. He wanted to make a prank on the organized clown. He sneaked behind him and tied his shoelaces together. Then he waited for the right moment.

The naughty clown raised his hand and said: "It was me! It was me! I did it for fun. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you. Are you okay?"

The organized clown sighed and said: "I'm okay, but you are very mean. You ruined my show. You should be more careful and respectful. You should apologize to the audience and the lion."

The naughty clown felt ashamed and said: "You are right. I'm sorry, everyone. I'm sorry, lion. I won't do it again. Please forgive me."

The audience clapped and cheered. The lion roared and shook his head. The organized clown smiled and said: "It's okay. We are friends. Let's finish our show together. Come on, help me up."

The naughty clown helped him up and hugged him. They joined the other clowns and continued their show. Tom and Mia enjoyed the rest of the circus. They learned a lesson: pranks are not always funny. They can hurt someone's feelings or cause trouble. They decided to be more kind and organized.

He said to Mia, "I have a bandage for you, Mia. It will make your knee better. But first, I have to clean it. It might sting a little, but it will be over soon. Can you be brave, Mia?"

Mia nodded and tried not to cry. Ben gently wiped the blood with the cloth. Mia winced, but she did not scream. Ben said, "Good job, Mia. You are very brave. Now, I will put the bandage on your knee. It will protect it and make it heal. The bandage is fragile, so you have to be careful not to tear it. OK?"

Mia nodded again and smiled. Ben wrapped the bandage around her knee and fixed it with a sticker. He said, "There, you are done. How do you feel, Mia?"

Mia said, "I feel better, Ben. Thank you for helping me. You are a good brother. You prepared the bandage for me. You are very kind."

Ben hugged Mia and said, "You are welcome, Mia. You are a good sister. I am glad you feel better. Let's go inside and tell Mom what happened. She will be proud of us."

They held hands and walked to the house. They were happy and proud. They had helped each other and learned a new word: prepare.

"Mom, look what I found! It's mine!" she said, holding the egg.

She put the egg on her bed and wrapped it with a blanket. She hoped it would hatch soon and give her a new friend. She did not know that the egg belonged to a snake.

The next day, Sara heard a cracking sound from the egg. She was excited and ran to see what was inside. She pulled the blanket and saw a baby snake. It was green and scaly and had sharp teeth. It hissed at her and tried to bite her.

"Help! Mom! There's a snake in my room!" Sara screamed, and ran out of the door.

Her mom came and saw the snake. She was scared and angry. She grabbed a broom and chased the snake away. She threw the egg shell in the trash.

"Sara, what were you thinking? That snake could have hurt you. You should have listened to me and left the egg alone. You were very stubborn and foolish," her mom said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know it was a snake. I thought it would be a nice friend. I was wrong. I won't be stubborn again," Sara said, and hugged her mom.

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I'm glad you're okay, Sara. I love you. But you have to learn to respect other lives and not take what is not yours. You have to be kind and obedient. Do you understand?"

"Yes, mom. I understand. I love you too," Sara said.

The moral of the story is: Don't be stubborn and greedy. Respect other lives and listen to your parents.

The bear told Bounce that he was upset because it was winter and he was very hungry. Bounce knew that he had to help the bear find some food. He hopped around the forest and found some berries and nuts for the bear to eat. The bear was very grateful and promised to be quiet from then on. Bounce was happy that he could help and the forest was peaceful once again.

The storm became worse and worse. The wind was so strong that it knocked down trees and power lines. Lily's house lost power and she was left in the dark. She was very sad and missed the lovely cloud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved muffins and would eat them every day. One day, she went to the bakery to buy a muffin. The baker said, "Hello Lily, what kind of muffin would you like today?" Lily replied, "I want a blueberry muffin, please."

The baker handed Lily the muffin and said, "That's a modest choice, Lily. Do you need help carrying it?" Lily said, "Yes, please. It's heavy." The baker lifted the muffin and handed it to Lily. She was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Baker!" 

Lily walked home with her muffin and saw her friend, Timmy. Timmy asked, "What do you have there, Lily?" Lily said, "I have a blueberry muffin. It's heavy, but the baker lifted it for me." Timmy asked, "Can I have a bite?" Lily said, "Sure, but just one bite." They shared the muffin and it was delicious.

Once upon a time, there was a happy squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to collect acorns to eat and play with. One day, Nutty found a big, shiny acorn and he was very cheerful. 

But then, Nutty's friend Sammy came along and said, "Oh no, Nutty! That acorn will spoil soon. You should eat it now before it's too late." 

Nutty didn't want to eat the acorn yet because he was enjoying playing with it. But Sammy was right, so Nutty decided to eat the acorn and save it from spoiling. 

After he ate the acorn, Nutty felt very full and happy. He thanked Sammy for reminding him to eat it before it spoiled. They both laughed and played together, enjoying the rest of their day in the cheerful sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and watching the helicopters in the sky. One day, she saw a helicopter land in the park near her house.

Excitedly, she ran over to see it. She saw a man get out and start rubbing the helicopter. "Why are you rubbing it?" she asked.

"I have to check it before I can fly it," the man replied.

Lily watched as the man got back in the helicopter and took off. But as he flew away, the helicopter suddenly crashed. Lily was sad and scared, but she knew that the man had done his best to make sure it was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she met a giant who was very big and tall. The giant was not scary, but charming and friendly. 

"Hello giant, what are you doing here?" asked Lily.

"I am looking for my lost ring," replied the giant.

Lily wanted to help the giant, so she searched the whole garden with him. Suddenly, they found the ring in a flower bed. The giant was very happy and thanked Lily for her help. 

"Thank you, Lily. You are a very kind girl," said the giant.

Lily smiled and replied, "It was my pleasure to help you, giant. Remember, even though you are big, you can still shrink in kindness." 

The giant was touched by Lily's words and promised to always be kind to others. From that day on, Lily and the giant became good friends and had many more adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in the water close to the shore. He had lots of friends, but he was scared of the unknown.

The wise old turtle thought for a moment and said, "We must swim together against the wave. That will prevent us from going to the shore."

Fin and his friends listened to the turtle and swam together against the wave. They were strong and stopped the wave from pushing them to the shore. They were happy and safe, and Fin was not scared of the unknown anymore.

Just when it was about to give up, it came across a friendly cow who had a wide mouth that it could fit into. The tooth was so happy and quickly hopped into the cow's mouth.

The tooth was so excited that it finally had a home! Every day the cow and the tooth laughed, chewed grass, and were always smiles.

The two were so happy together, and the tooth finally found a place it could call home.

Once there was a mole who was very ugly. He looked around for a place to lie down and rest but it was so hard to find a cozy spot. All the other animals laughed at him and thought he was so funny! That made the mole feel very sad.

He decided to go find a new home. He searched and searched until he finally came across a warm patch of grass. He dug down deep and made a little hole. Now he could lie down and be cozy and safe.

But soon, some of the other animals noticed the mole and started to laugh at him again. They said that his hole was too tiny and that he was too ugly. The mole was so embarrassed, so he quickly climbed out of his hole and ran away.

He wanted to find somewhere else to lie down and be safe, but now he was just too scared to try. So he decided to build a big and strong wall around his cozy patch of grass. That way he could lie down and nobody would ever laugh at him again.

Once upon a time there was a village of happy people. They were always kind to each other and looked out for one another. Every day they would work in the fields, play games and gossip.

She took the match and walked to the radio. She did not see her mom in the kitchen. She did not hear her dad in the living room. She was alone with the radio and the match. She scratched the match on the box and it lit up. She felt the heat on her fingers. She brought the match close to the radio.

"Hey, what are you doing?" a voice said behind her. It was her big brother, Tom. He saw Lily with the match and the radio. He ran to her and grabbed the match from her hand. He blew it out and threw it in the trash. He was angry and scared. "Are you crazy? You could have burned the house down! You could have hurt yourself or the radio! Don't you know that matches and radios don't match?"

Lily started to cry. She did not mean to do anything bad. She just wanted to play and explore. She did not know that matches and radios don't match. She did not know that fire could be so dangerous. She hugged her radio and said sorry. She said sorry to Tom too.

Tom calmed down and hugged Lily back. He said sorry for yelling at her. He said he loved her and he wanted her to be safe. He said he would show her how the radio worked and what was inside. He said they could listen to music or stories together. He said they could find other things that match, like colors or shapes or sounds. He said they could have fun without matches. Lily smiled and nodded. She liked Tom and she liked her radio. She learned a new lesson that day. She learned that matches and radios don't match, but brothers and sisters do.

Tom said, "No, Lily. The pond is deep and wet. We might fall in. We can look at the fish from here."

Lily was sad. She wanted to see the fish better. She saw a small fish near the edge of the pond. It was red and shiny. Lily thought it was pretty. She said, "Look, Tom. A small fish. It is so cute. I want to say hello to it."

Tom said, "Be careful, Lily. Don't go too close. The fish might swim away."

Lily did not listen. She walked to the pond. She bent down to touch the small fish. She said, "Hello, fish. I am Lily. Do you want to be my friend?"

But the small fish was not a fish. It was a toy. It had a button on its back. When Lily touched it, the toy made a loud noise. It said, "Surprise! I am not a fish. I am a robot. Beep beep boop."

Lily was scared. She jumped back. She screamed, "Aaaah! It is not a fish. It is a robot. It talks. It scares me."

Tom ran to Lily. He hugged her. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. It is just a toy. Someone left it here. It is not real. It cannot hurt you."

Lily calmed down. She looked at the toy. She said, "It is a toy? It is not a fish? It is a robot?"

Tom said, "Yes, Lily. It is a toy. It is not a fish. It is a robot. It is a surprise."

Lily said, "It is a surprise. It is a funny surprise. It makes me laugh. Ha ha ha."

Tom said, "It makes me laugh too. Ha ha ha."

They laughed together. They played with the toy. They had fun. They liked the surprise.

But then, something went wrong. The hose got stuck. The water did not stop. It sprayed everywhere. It made a big puddle. It hit the flowers and the fence and the window.

"Stop! Stop!" Ben and Lily shouted. But the hose did not listen.

They tried to pull the hose. They tried to twist the button. They tried to run away. But the hose was too strong. It followed them like a snake. It was enormous.

"Help! Help!" Ben and Lily cried.

Mama heard them. She came out of the house. She saw the mess. She saw the hose. She was not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asked.

"Sorry, Mama. The hose is bad. It won't stop," Ben said.

She took the hose from Ben. She looked at the button. She saw the problem. The button was broken. She fixed it. The water stopped.

"Phew!" Ben and Lily said.

They like to play and jump and make noises. They are not like sharks, who are mean and hungry and bite."

"Can we play with the dolphins, dad?" they asked.

Ben and Lily agreed and thanked their dad. They went back to the sand and watched the dolphins with wonder and joy. They forgot about the shark and their fear. They learned something new and had a great day.

One day, they saw a big jar of jelly on the kitchen table. They loved jelly and wanted to eat some. But their mom said, "No, this jelly is for the party tomorrow. You can have some then. Now go and play."

Tim and Sam were sad. They wanted jelly now. They looked at each other and had a bad idea. They waited until their mom went to the bathroom. Then they ran to the kitchen and grabbed the jar of jelly. They ran outside with it and hid behind the slide.

They opened the jar and started to eat the jelly with their fingers. It was sweet and sticky and yummy. They ate and ate and ate. They did not see Spot coming. Spot smelled the jelly and wanted some too. He jumped on them and licked their faces and hands. He knocked over the jar and spilled the jelly on the ground.

Tim and Sam were scared. They saw the mess they made. They saw their mom coming. They knew they were in trouble. They felt nervous and sorry.

Their mom saw them and the jelly. She was angry and sad. She said, "What did you do? You were naughty and greedy. You wasted the jelly and made a mess. You did not listen to me. You have to clean up and go to your room. No jelly for you tomorrow."

Tim and Sam cried. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were wrong. We should have waited. We should have obeyed. We learned our lesson. Please forgive us."

Their mom hugged them and said, "I forgive you, but you still have to face the consequences. You have to clean up and go to your room. Maybe next time you will think before you act. Now go and rest. You ate too much jelly. You might have a tummy ache."

Tim and Sam nodded. They cleaned up and went to their room. They felt sick and sad. They wished they had not eaten the jelly. They learned that being patient and respectful is better than being selfish and sneaky. They hoped their mom would still love them. They hugged each other and rested.

Tommy was a big boy who liked to play with his cars and trucks. He had many toys, but his favorite was a red fire truck that made a loud siren sound. He always took it with him when he went to the park or to his grandma's house.

One day, Tommy's mom said they had to go to the doctor for a check-up. Tommy did not like the doctor. He was afraid of the needles and the cold stethoscope. He did not want to leave his fire truck at home. He begged his mom to let him bring it with him.

"Please, mom, please. I need my fire truck. It makes me feel brave," Tommy said.

"Okay, Tommy, you can bring your fire truck, but you have to hold it tight and not lose it. The doctor is very nice and he will not hurt you. He just wants to make sure you are healthy and strong," his mom said.

Tommy nodded and hugged his fire truck. He felt a little better. He and his mom got in the car and drove to the doctor's office.

When they got there, Tommy saw many other kids waiting in the lobby. Some of them were crying, some of them were laughing, some of them were reading books or playing with toys. Tommy clutched his fire truck and followed his mom to the receptionist.

"Hello, we have an appointment for Tommy Smith," his mom said.

"Hello, welcome. Please take a seat and we will call you soon," the receptionist said.

Tommy and his mom sat down on a couch. Tommy looked around and saw a big fish tank with colorful fish swimming inside. He liked the fish. They looked peaceful and happy. He wondered if they ever got sick or had to go to the doctor.

He was so busy watching the fish that he did not notice a little girl sitting next to him. She had curly hair and a pink dress. She also had a big teddy bear in her arms. She smiled at Tommy and reached for his fire truck.

"Can I play with your fire truck?" she asked.

Tommy was startled. He did not want to share his fire truck. It was his and it made him feel brave. He pulled it away from the girl and said, "No, it's mine. Go away."

The girl frowned and started to cry. She hugged her teddy bear and said, "You are mean. I just wanted to play with you."

Tommy felt bad. He did not mean to make the girl cry. He liked to play with other kids, but he was scared of the doctor and he did not want to lose his fire truck. He did not know what to say.

Before he could say anything, his mom said, "Tommy, it's your turn. The doctor is ready to see you. Come on, let's go."

Tommy got up and followed his mom. He looked back at the girl and saw her still crying. He felt a pang in his stomach. He wished he had been nicer to her. He wished he had said sorry. He wished he had let her play with his fire truck.

He wondered if the doctor would make him cry too. He wondered if he would ever see the girl again. He wondered if she would ever forgive him. He wondered if he would ever feel peaceful and happy like the fish.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Lily went first and slid down fast. She laughed and clapped her hands. Tom followed her and slid down too. He smiled and said, "That was fun!"

They saw a man with a cart. He had many things in it. He had balloons, toys, and chocolate. Lily and Tom liked chocolate. They went to the man and asked, "Can we have some chocolate, please?"

The man looked at them and frowned. He said, "No, you can't. You are filthy. You have dirt on your faces and clothes. You need to wash before you eat chocolate. Go away!"

Lily and Tom felt sad and angry. They did not think they were filthy. They thought they were just having fun. They did not want to wash. They wanted chocolate. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They waited until the man was busy with another customer. Then they sneaked to his cart and grabbed some chocolate. They ran away as fast as they could. They did not care if the man saw them or shouted at them. They were happy.

They found a bench and sat down. They opened the chocolate and gave some to each other. They ate it and licked their fingers. It was sweet and yummy. They said, "This is the best chocolate ever!" They hugged and giggled. They did not mind being filthy. They were friends.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But today, they are bored. They have nothing new to do.

"Let's go outside and find something fun," Sara says to Ben.

"OK, but we have to be careful. Mom and Dad are at work. They told us not to go far," Ben says.

They put on their shoes and coats and go out the door. They see a big hill near their house. They wonder what is on the other side.

"Let's go up the hill and see," Sara says.

They start to climb the hill. It is hard work. They get tired and thirsty. They wish they had brought some water and snacks.

They reach the top of the hill. They see a big lake with ducks and fish. They also see a small boat with oars.

"Wow, look at that! Let's go on the boat and have an adventure," Sara says.

She runs to the boat and jumps in. Ben follows her. They grab the oars and start to row.

They have fun on the boat. They see the ducks and fish. They pretend they are pirates and explorers. They forget about their mom and dad and their home.

But then, the wind starts to blow. The water gets rough. The boat rocks and shakes. Sara and Ben are scared.

"Help! Help! We want to go back!" they cry.

They try to row back to the shore, but they can't. The wind is too strong. They are in trouble.

They see a man on the shore. He has a big hat and a long coat. He hears their cries and sees their boat.

He runs to the lake and gets another boat. He rows to Sara and Ben and helps them get in his boat. He rows them back to the shore.

He is angry and worried. He asks them who they are and where they live. He tells them they are very naughty and foolish. He tells them they could have drowned or got lost.

He takes them to their house and knocks on the door. Their mom and dad are home. They are surprised and relieved to see them. They hug them and thank the man.

They also scold them and punish them. They tell them they are not allowed to go outside without permission. They tell them they have to stay in their room and do their homework.

Sara and Ben are sorry and sad. They wish they had not gone on the boat. They wish they had listened to their mom and dad. They learn their lesson. They never go on the boat again.
